countries.name: Aruba
countries.triviaFact: Constant trade winds bend the native Divi-divi trees toward the southwest across this sunny southern Caribbean island. Unlike many of its neighbors, it sits outside the main hurricane belt and has a dry, cactus-filled interior. Visitors can explore Arikok National Park to see ancient cave drawings left by the indigenous Caquetío people.

countries.name: Afghanistan
countries.triviaFact: High mountain ranges like the Hindu Kush cover most of this landlocked country at the crossroads of Central and South Asia. For centuries, Silk Road caravans traveled through its steep mountain passes carrying silk, spices, and priceless blue lapis lazuli stones mined in the northeast. Famous historical sites include the giant cliff niches of Bamiyan and the blue-tiled shrine in Mazar-i-Sharif.

countries.name: Angola
countries.triviaFact: Stretching along the southwestern coast of Africa, this large country combines Atlantic beaches with high central plateaus and tropical forests in the north. In the dry southern desert of Namibe, the strange Welwitschia plant grows just two leaves that can live for over a thousand years. Travelers also marvel at the steep hairpins of the Leba Pass mountain road and the wide cascades of Kalandula Falls.

countries.name: Anguilla
countries.triviaFact: Flat coral and limestone form this quiet island territory at the northern end of the Lesser Antilles. Thirty-three white sand beaches and clear turquoise waters surround the main island and its tiny offshore cays. Wooden sailboat racing is the national sport here, and locals gather on the beach for big regattas during summer holidays.

countries.name: Åland Islands
countries.triviaFact: More than six thousand rocky islands make up this self-governing archipelago at the entrance to the Gulf of Bothnia. Although it belongs to Finland, the residents speak Swedish as their sole official language. Under an international treaty signed in 1856, the entire group of islands remains a neutral zone with no military forces allowed.

countries.name: Albania
countries.triviaFact: Steep mountains cover most of this Balkan country along the Adriatic and Ionian seas. During the Cold War, a secretive government built more than 170,000 concrete bunkers across every valley, mountain pass, and beach. Today, travelers come for the sunny southern coast, the stone houses of Gjirokastër, and the wild Vjosa River.

countries.name: Andorra
countries.triviaFact: Tucked high in the Pyrenees mountains between France and Spain, this tiny principality has no airport or train station of its own. Since 1278, it has been ruled jointly by two foreign co-princes: a Spanish bishop and the head of state of France. Catalan is the official language, and winter ski resorts and duty-free shops drive the local economy.

countries.name: United Arab Emirates
countries.triviaFact: Seven desert principalities along the Persian Gulf united in 1971 to form this wealthy Middle Eastern federation. Before oil was discovered in the 1950s, local coastal towns relied on wooden dhows that dove for natural pearls and traded spices across the sea. Today, its cities feature the 828-meter Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building, and the white marble domes of the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque.

countries.name: Argentina
countries.triviaFact: Running down the eastern side of South America, this huge country stretches from subtropical jungles in the north to subpolar glaciers in Patagonia. It contains both the highest mountain peak in the Western Hemisphere, Aconcagua, and the thunderous waterfalls of Iguazú. The nation is also famous around the world for tango music, vast cattle ranches on the Pampas plains, and mate tea.

countries.name: Armenia
countries.triviaFact: In the year 301 AD, this mountainous Caucasus nation became the very first country in the world to adopt Christianity as its state religion. Ancient stone monasteries like Geghard and Tatev sit carved into deep rocky gorges below the snow-covered peak of Mount Ararat. The capital city is one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities and is built from pink volcanic rock.

countries.name: American Samoa
countries.triviaFact: Five rugged volcanic islands and two coral atolls make up this unincorporated territory in the South Pacific. Rainmaker Mountain rises steeply above the capital, sheltering one of the deepest and best-protected natural harbors in the region. Most land is still owned collectively by extended families under a traditional Polynesian social system that dates back thousands of years.

countries.name: Antarctica
countries.triviaFact: Thick ice sheets averaging two kilometers deep cover nearly all of this vast southern continent, holding about seventy percent of the world's fresh water. It is the coldest, windiest, and driest continent on Earth, with no permanent human residents or native land mammals. Under a 1959 international treaty, the entire landmass is set aside as a peaceful reserve for scientific research.

countries.name: French Southern and Antarctic Lands
countries.officialName: Territory of the French Southern and Antarctic Lands
countries.triviaFact: Scattered across the stormy southern Indian Ocean, these remote volcanic islands have no permanent civilian population. Only small teams of scientists and support staff live on bases among the wind-swept rocks of Kerguelen, Crozet, and Amsterdam islands. Millions of king penguins, albatrosses, and elephant seals breed along the cold, rocky shores every year.

countries.name: Antigua and Barbuda
countries.triviaFact: Locals proudly say this two-island Caribbean nation has 365 beaches, offering a different stretch of sand for every single day of the year. The larger island is famous for English Harbour and Nelson's Dockyard, the only Georgian-era naval dockyard in the world still in use by yachts today. Its smaller sister island is a flat coral sanctuary known for pink sand beaches and a huge colony of magnificent frigatebirds.

countries.name: Australia
countries.triviaFact: Covering an entire continent between the Indian and Pacific oceans, this is the sixth-largest country in the world by area. Because it was separated from other landmasses for millions of years, most of its native mammals are marsupials like kangaroos, koalas, and wombats. Famous natural wonders include the Great Barrier Reef, the red desert rock of Uluru, and a vast dry interior called the Outback.

countries.name: Austria
countries.triviaFact: The towering peaks of the Alps cover more than sixty percent of this landlocked Central European country. For centuries, its capital on the Danube River served as the center of the Habsburg Empire and the world capital of classical music under composers like Mozart, Haydn, and Strauss. At Hallstatt in the central mountains, people have mined underground rock salt for more than seven thousand years.

countries.name: Azerbaijan
countries.triviaFact: Sitting where Eastern Europe and Western Asia meet along the Caspian Sea, this country is famous for its underground oil and natural gas reserves. Gas seeping through hillside rock keeps natural flames burning day and night in the rain and snow at Yanar Dag. The country also has around four hundred bubbling mud volcanoes, more than any other place on Earth.

countries.name: Burundi
countries.triviaFact: Green hills and high plateaus cover this small landlocked country in the Great Rift Valley of East Africa. Its southwestern border runs along Lake Tanganyika, which is the second-deepest and longest freshwater lake in the world. The country is famous for the Royal Drummers of Gishora, who balance heavy hollowed-out tree trunks on their heads and play complex rhythms.

countries.name: Belgium
countries.triviaFact: Divided mainly between Dutch-speaking Flanders in the north and French-speaking Wallonia in the south, this Western European kingdom sits at the heart of European politics. Its capital hosts the main headquarters of both the European Union and NATO. People around the world know the country for its medieval canal towns like Bruges, fine chocolates, comic strip art, and hundreds of traditional beer styles.

countries.name: Benin
countries.triviaFact: Extending north from a short Atlantic coastline in West Africa, this country was once home to a powerful royal kingdom famous for its all-female palace guard. It is also the birthplace of Vodun, a traditional religion that later shaped spiritual practices across the Caribbean and the Americas. On Lake Nokoué near the coast, thousands of people live in Ganvié, a remarkable town built entirely on wooden stilts over the water.

countries.name: Burkina Faso
countries.triviaFact: Flat savannas and dry Sahelian plains stretch across this landlocked country in West Africa. Its name translates from local languages as the Land of Upright People, adopted in 1984 to replace its old colonial name. Every two years, the capital hosts FESPACO, the largest and most prestigious film festival on the African continent.

countries.name: Bangladesh
countries.triviaFact: Three mighty rivers, the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna, come together here to form the largest river delta in the world. Over 170 million people live across these fertile green plains, making it one of the most densely populated nations on Earth. Along the southern coast grows the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest and home to the royal striped tiger.

countries.name: Bulgaria
countries.triviaFact: Founded in 681 AD south of the Danube River, this Balkan nation is one of the oldest countries in Europe to keep its original name. Scholars here developed the Cyrillic alphabet during the 9th century, which is now used by hundreds of millions of people across Eurasia. In a sunny central valley south of the Balkan Mountains, farmers harvest acres of fragrant damask roses to produce most of the world's rose oil.

countries.name: Bahrain
countries.triviaFact: More than thirty natural and man-made islands make up this small Arab kingdom in the Persian Gulf. Four thousand years ago, the main island was a major Bronze Age trading hub and still holds tens of thousands of ancient stone burial mounds. It was the first place on the Arabian side of the gulf to strike oil in 1932 and connects to Saudi Arabia via a 25-kilometer bridge causeway.

countries.name: Bahamas
countries.triviaFact: Around seven hundred low coral islands and more than two thousand tiny cays stretch across the clear shallow waters of the Atlantic just southeast of Florida. In 1492, Christopher Columbus made his very first landfall in the Americas on one of these outer islands. Visitors come to swim in crystal-clear blue holes, dive along barrier reefs, and see famous wild pigs swimming in the sea at Exuma.

countries.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
countries.triviaFact: Rugged Dinaric Alps and green river valleys shape this heart-shaped Balkan country, which has just twenty kilometers of coastline on the Adriatic Sea. For centuries, it has been a meeting place of Ottoman Islamic, Catholic, and Orthodox Christian traditions. Its most famous landmark is the 16th-century arched stone bridge in Mostar, where local divers leap more than twenty meters into the cold Neretva River.

countries.name: Saint Barthélemy
countries.triviaFact: Red-roofed villas and rocky hills surround the yacht-filled harbor of this small volcanic island in the northern Caribbean. Unlike neighboring French islands, France traded this island to Sweden in 1784 in exchange for trading rights in Gothenburg, and Sweden ruled it for nearly a century. That history still shows in the capital's name, Gustavia, which honors Swedish King Gustav III.

countries.name: Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha
countries.officialName: Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha
countries.triviaFact: Spread across the vast South Atlantic Ocean, this remote British territory consists of three volcanic island groups separated by thousands of kilometers of open water. Napoleon Bonaparte spent the last six years of his life in exile on the main island after his defeat at Waterloo in 1815. Farther south lies the most remote inhabited archipelago on Earth, reachable only by a six-day boat trip from South Africa.

countries.name: Belarus
countries.triviaFact: Thick forests, flat marshes, and thousands of streams cover this landlocked country in Eastern Europe. On its western border lies Białowieża Forest, one of the last remaining tracts of the ancient primeval woodland that once stretched across the European plain. That forest is the main sanctuary for the heavy European bison, and historic castles with red-brick towers still stand at Mir and Nesvizh.

countries.name: Belize
countries.triviaFact: Tucked along the Caribbean coast of Central America, this is the only country in the region where English is the official language. Offshore runs the longest unbroken living barrier reef in the Western Hemisphere, which surrounds the famous circular sinkhole known as the Great Blue Hole. Inland, dense tropical jungles shelter jaguars and tall stone Maya temple pyramids like Caracol and Xunantunich.

countries.name: Bermuda
countries.triviaFact: Sitting alone in the North Atlantic Ocean about a thousand kilometers east of North Carolina, this fishhook-shaped archipelago consists of over 180 small coral islands linked by bridges. Crushed shells of tiny red sea creatures mix with white sand to give its south-shore beaches a soft pink glow. Because the islands have no rivers or freshwater lakes, every house is built with a stepped white limestone roof that catches rainwater and channels it into an underground tank.

countries.name: Bolivia
countries.triviaFact: Cut off from the Pacific Ocean after a 19th-century war, this high-altitude South American nation sits partly on the wide Andean plateau known as the Altiplano. It shares Lake Titicaca, the world's highest navigable lake, and holds the seat of government at La Paz, the highest administrative capital in the world. In the southwest lies Salar de Uyuni, the world's largest salt flat, which turns into a giant sky mirror after summer rains.

countries.name: Caribbean Netherlands
countries.triviaFact: Three very different islands in the Lesser Antilles make up these special overseas municipalities of the Kingdom of the Low Countries. The southern island near Venezuela is famous for pink flamingos, salt pans, and shore-entry scuba diving reefs. Nearly eight hundred kilometers away in the north sit the other two islands, including the steep volcanic cone of Saba, which holds the highest peak under royal jurisdiction.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.triviaFact: Covering nearly half of South America, this is the fifth-largest country in the world and the only nation in the Americas where Portuguese is the official language. It holds the majority of the Amazon River basin, which carries more water than any other river on Earth and shelters unmatched tropical wildlife. From the modernist airplane-shaped layout of its highland capital to the beaches and giant Christ statue of Rio de Janeiro, the country is also world-famous for Carnival samba and football.

countries.name: Barbados
countries.triviaFact: Unlike the volcanic islands of the eastern Caribbean arc, this easternmost island was pushed up out of the Atlantic Ocean from ancient coral limestone. Sugarcane plantations here began distilling Mount Gay rum in 1703, making it the oldest commercial rum producer in the world. In 2021, the country officially transitioned from a constitutional monarchy into the world's newest parliamentary republic.

countries.name: Brunei
countries.officialName: Nation of Brunei, the Abode of Peace
countries.triviaFact: Surrounded by Malaysian territory on the northern coast of Borneo, this small sultanate owes its high wealth to offshore oil and natural gas fields. Because of oil revenues, citizens pay no personal income tax and receive free education and healthcare. In the capital, tens of thousands of people still live in Kampong Ayer, a century-old community of wooden houses, schools, and mosques built on stilts over the river.

countries.name: Bhutan
countries.triviaFact: High in the eastern Himalayas between China and India, this Buddhist kingdom measures its progress by Gross National Happiness rather than just economic output. Strict laws require at least sixty percent of the land to stay under forest cover at all times, making it one of the world's only carbon-negative countries. Its most iconic landmark is Paro Taktsang, the Tiger's Nest Monastery, which clings to a sheer cliff face nine hundred meters above the valley floor.

countries.name: Bouvet Island
countries.triviaFact: Covered almost entirely by thick glaciers and steep black volcanic cliffs, this tiny island in the subantarctic South Atlantic is the most remote uninhabited island on Earth. The nearest landmass is Antarctica, more than 1,600 kilometers to the south, with no human settlements anywhere nearby. Norway claims the frozen island as a dependency and runs an automated weather station there to track southern ocean storms.

countries.name: Botswana
countries.triviaFact: Roughly seventy percent of this landlocked Southern African country is covered by the sandy savanna of the Kalahari Desert. In the northwest, the Okavango River never reaches the sea and instead fans out into the desert sands to create a huge seasonal wetland delta. This inland delta attracts the largest remaining herds of African elephants on the continent alongside lions, hippos, and painted wild dogs.

countries.name: Central African Republic
countries.triviaFact: Sitting right in the middle of the continent, this landlocked nation stretches from dry northern savannas down to thick equatorial rainforests along the Ubangi River. In the southwestern jungle reserve of Dzanga-Sangha, dozens of forest elephants and western lowland gorillas gather in mineral-rich mud clearings every day. Despite having rich deposits of diamonds, gold, and timber, it remains one of the least developed countries in the world.

countries.name: Canada
countries.triviaFact: Stretching from the Atlantic to the Pacific and north into the Arctic Ocean, this is the second-largest country in the world by total area. Its rugged shores form the longest coastline of any nation on Earth, and its glacier-carved interior holds more freshwater lakes than the rest of the world combined. The country is officially bilingual in English and French, famous for maple syrup, ice hockey, and the dramatic peaks of the Rocky Mountains.

countries.name: Cocos (Keeling) Islands
countries.triviaFact: Twenty-seven small coral islands form two ring-shaped atolls in the eastern Indian Ocean midway between Australia and Sri Lanka. When Charles Darwin visited these lagoons aboard the HMS Beagle in 1836, studying their coral rings helped him prove how volcanic islands sink to form coral atolls. Today, only two of the islands are inhabited, with a Malay-descended community on Home Island and a mainland Australian community on West Island.

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.triviaFact: Surrounded by neighbors in the heart of the Alps, this country has not fought in an international war since 1815 and maintains a strict policy of armed neutrality. It has four national languages, German, French, Italian, and Romansh, and lets citizens vote directly on laws several times a year in national referendums. Famous around the world for precision watchmaking, Alpine railways, and chocolate, it also hosts the European headquarters of the United Nations and the CERN particle physics lab.

countries.name: Chile
countries.triviaFact: Squeezed between the high Andes mountains and the Pacific Ocean, this ribbon-shaped South American country is over 4,300 kilometers long but averages less than 180 kilometers wide. Its far north holds the bone-dry Atacama Desert, where some weather stations have never recorded rain and giant telescopes study the night sky. In the far south, icy fjords and granite towers rise in Patagonia, while remote Easter Island in Polynesia is famous for its giant carved stone heads.

countries.name: China
countries.triviaFact: Stretching from the Pacific coast to the high plateaus of Tibet and the deserts of Central Asia, this is one of the world's oldest continuous civilizations. Ancient rulers connected thousands of miles of stone walls and watchtowers across northern mountain ridges to build the Great Wall, and buried an army of thousands of life-sized clay soldiers in Xi'an. Paper, printing, gunpowder, and the magnetic compass were all invented here centuries ago.

countries.name: Ivory Coast
countries.triviaFact: Small family farms across the tropical forests of this West African nation grow more than forty percent of the world's cocoa beans. Although Abidjan on the Atlantic shore is the largest city and main port, the official capital was moved inland to Yamoussoukro in 1983. Rising above Yamoussoukro is the Basilica of Our Lady of Peace, whose giant dome makes it the largest Christian church building in the world by area.

countries.name: Cameroon
countries.triviaFact: People often call this Central African nation 'Africa in Miniature' because its landscapes include coastal beaches, dense rainforests, mountains, and dry northern savannas. Rising right next to the Atlantic coast is an active volcano that stands over four thousand meters tall and receives some of the heaviest rainfall on Earth. Both French and English serve as official languages alongside more than two hundred local indigenous languages.

countries.name: DR Congo
countries.triviaFact: Straddling the equator in Central Africa, this is the second-largest country on the continent and holds more than half of Africa's tropical rainforests. The mighty river that gives the country its name curves through the basin in a giant arc and is the deepest river on Earth. In the eastern mountains, Virunga National Park protects rare mountain gorillas and the glowing lava lake inside Mount Nyiragongo.

countries.name: Congo
countries.triviaFact: Dense equatorial rainforests and vast carbon-storing peat swamps cover much of this Central African nation. Its capital sits on the northern bank of the wide Malebo Pool directly across the river from Kinshasa, making the two cities the closest pair of national capitals in the world outside Rome. In the remote northern forests of Nouabalé-Ndoki, western lowland gorillas and forest elephants live in areas untouched by logging roads.

countries.name: Cook Islands
countries.triviaFact: Fifteen small islands lie scattered across two million square kilometers of the South Pacific Ocean between Tahiti and Tonga. Although the islands are self-governing, their residents hold New Zealand citizenship and use the New Zealand dollar. The southern island of Rarotonga is ringed by a shallow lagoon and jagged green volcanic peaks, while Aitutaki is famous for its bright turquoise coral lagoon.

countries.name: Colombia
countries.triviaFact: Located at the northwestern corner of South America, this is the only country on the continent with coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea. Because the Andes split into three separate mountain ranges here, the diverse habitats support more species of birds and orchids than any other country on Earth. It is also world-famous for high-altitude Arabica coffee farms and produces most of the world's finest green emeralds.

countries.name: Comoros
countries.triviaFact: Three volcanic islands in the northern Mozambique Channel between Madagascar and mainland Africa form this island nation. Farmers grow fragrant ylang-ylang flowers, vanilla, and cloves on the volcanic slopes, earning the archipelago the nickname of the Perfume Isles. Deep in the ocean waters around the main island live coelacanths, rare lobe-finned fish once thought to have gone extinct with the dinosaurs sixty-five million years ago.

countries.name: Cape Verde
countries.triviaFact: Ten volcanic islands lie scattered in the Atlantic Ocean about six hundred kilometers off the westernmost tip of Africa. Uninhabited until Portuguese sailors arrived in the 15th century, the islands developed a vibrant Creole culture and the soulful, melancholic music style called morna. On the island of Fogo, villagers farm coffee and grapes inside the giant caldera of an active volcano that towers nearly three thousand meters above the sea.

countries.name: Costa Rica
countries.triviaFact: Bridging North and South America between the Pacific and Caribbean coasts, this small country shelters roughly five percent of the world's known plant and animal species. After a brief civil war in 1948, the government permanently abolished its military and redirected defense spending into schools, healthcare, and nature parks. Today, more than a quarter of the land is protected in national parks, and almost all of its electricity comes from renewable hydropower, wind, and geothermal energy.

countries.name: Cuba
countries.triviaFact: Shaped like a long crocodile at the entrance to the Gulf of Mexico, this is the largest island in the Caribbean. Rolling tobacco farms in the limestone valley of Viñales produce the world's most famous hand-rolled cigars, while colorful 1950s cars still cruise the seaside boulevard of the capital. Its music, from son and mambo to salsa, has shaped popular music across the entire world.

countries.name: Curaçao
countries.triviaFact: Brightly painted Dutch colonial buildings line the waterfront of this sunny island in the southern Caribbean just north of Venezuela. A historic wooden floating bridge called the Queen Emma swings open sideways several times a day to let ocean ships enter the harbor. Locals speak Papiamentu, a melodic creole language blending Portuguese, Spanish, Dutch, and African roots, and export the famous blue liqueur made from dried bitter orange peels.

countries.name: Christmas Island
countries.triviaFact: Named by an English sea captain who sailed past on December 25, 1643, this remote Australian island sits in the Indian Ocean south of Java. Almost two-thirds of the island is protected as a national park covered in tall tropical rainforest. Every year at the start of the wet season, more than forty million bright red land crabs march out of the forest to lay their eggs in the sea, closing roads across the island.

countries.name: Cayman Islands
countries.triviaFact: Three low-lying coral islands in the western Caribbean form this British Overseas Territory, which actually sits on the peaks of a giant underwater mountain range next to a deep ocean trench. With no direct taxes on income or companies, the capital has grown into one of the largest banking and financial centers in the world. Offshore, visitors wade on shallow sandbars to feed friendly wild southern stingrays and dive along steep underwater coral walls.

countries.name: Cyprus
countries.triviaFact: Positioned in the eastern Mediterranean Sea south of Anatolia, this sunny island has been a crossroads of Greek, Roman, Crusader, and Ottoman history for thousands of years. Ancient Greek mythology named its rocky southern shore as the birthplace of Aphrodite, the goddess of love, and Copper took its Latin name from the island's rich ancient mines. Since 1974, a United Nations buffer zone has run right through the walled center of its capital, making it the last divided capital city in the world.

countries.name: Czechia
countries.triviaFact: Ringed by low mountain ranges in Central Europe, this landlocked nation has a rich history of medieval towns, glassmaking, and castles. Its capital is called the City of a Hundred Spires and features a 14th-century stone bridge and the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Having invented golden pilsner lager in the city of Plzeň in 1842, the country leads the world in beer consumed per person every year.

countries.name: Germany
countries.triviaFact: With more than eighty million residents, this Central European nation has the largest population and biggest economy in the European Union. In the 15th century, Johannes Gutenberg changed world history here by inventing the movable-type printing press, and centuries later Karl Benz built the first modern gasoline automobile. From the fairytale towers of Neuschwanstein Castle and the trails of the Black Forest to the Brandenburg Gate, the country has shaped science, philosophy, and classical music.

countries.name: Djibouti
countries.triviaFact: Located at the southern entrance to the Red Sea on the Horn of Africa, this small country controls one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Because of its strategic port, several foreign powers, including the United States, France, China, and Japan, operate military bases here side by side. Inland lies Lake Assal, a crater lake ringed by white salt crystals that sits 155 meters below sea level, making it the lowest point in Africa.

countries.name: Dominica
countries.triviaFact: Unlike its flatter neighbors, this rugged island in the eastern Caribbean is covered in steep volcanic peaks, thick rainforests, and 365 rivers. Hikers trek through the steaming Valley of Desolation to reach the Boiling Lake, a flooded volcanic fumarole filled with bubbling gray water. The eastern coast is also home to the Kalinago Territory, the only remaining reserve of the indigenous Carib people who gave the Caribbean Sea its name.

countries.name: Denmark
countries.triviaFact: Made up of the Jutland peninsula and more than four hundred islands, this flat Nordic kingdom bridges mainland Europe and Scandinavia. It has one of the oldest continuous monarchies in the world, dating back more than a thousand years to Viking kings like Gorm the Old and Harald Bluetooth. Known for inventing colorful interlocking plastic toy bricks, offshore wind turbines, and a cozy way of life called hygge, the country also includes autonomous Greenland and the Faroe Islands.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
countries.triviaFact: Sharing the island of Hispaniola with Haiti, this country covers the eastern two-thirds of the island and features both the highest mountain peak and the lowest point in the Caribbean. In 1496, Spanish settlers founded the capital on the southern coast, where the first cathedral, university, and stone fortress of the Americas still stand. Merengue and bachata music fill the streets, and baseball is a national passion that has produced hundreds of major-league stars.

countries.name: Algeria
countries.triviaFact: Covering nearly 2.4 million square kilometers from the Mediterranean coast deep into the heart of the Sahara, this is the largest country in Africa by land area. More than eighty percent of the territory is desert, including the sandstone plateaus of Tassili n'Ajjer, where prehistoric cave paintings show that the Sahara was once green savanna filled with giraffes and hippos. Along the northern coast stand remarkably preserved Roman cities like Timgad and Tipasa alongside the steep whitewashed alleys of the Casbah.

countries.name: Ecuador
countries.triviaFact: Named after the equator that runs right across its northern highlands, this South American country packs four distinct worlds into a compact area: the Amazon jungle, the Andes mountains, the Pacific coast, and the Galápagos Islands. Because Earth bulges outward at the equator, the snow-capped peak of Mount Chimborazo here is actually the farthest point from the center of the planet. A thousand kilometers offshore, the volcanic Galápagos Islands inspired Charles Darwin's theory of evolution with their giant tortoises and marine iguanas.

countries.name: Egypt
countries.triviaFact: For more than five thousand years, life in this northeastern African nation has depended on the fertile green ribbon of the Nile River flowing through the desert. Near the modern capital stand the Great Sphinx and the Pyramids of Giza, the only surviving wonder of the ancient world, while huge stone temples line the river farther south at Luxor and Abu Simbel. In the east, the man-made Suez Canal cuts across the desert isthmus to connect the Mediterranean Sea directly with the Red Sea.

countries.name: Eritrea
countries.triviaFact: Running along the western shore of the Red Sea in the Horn of Africa, this country includes both a hot coastal plain and cool central highlands. Its capital sits more than two thousand meters above sea level and is a UNESCO World Heritage site famous for early 20th-century modernist cinemas, cafes, and service stations. Offshore lies the Dahlak Archipelago, a group of over two hundred mostly uninhabited coral islands known for pearl fisheries and marine life.

countries.name: Western Sahara
countries.triviaFact: Flat gravel plains and shifting sand dunes stretch across this sparsely populated desert territory on the Atlantic coast of Northwest Africa. Its rich coastal waters are among the most productive fishing grounds in the region, and an enormous open-pit mine at Bou Craa sends phosphate rock to the coast on the world's longest conveyor belt. A 2,700-kilometer sand wall built during the 1980s divides the territory between Moroccan-administered areas in the west and Sahrawi-controlled zones in the east.

countries.name: Spain
countries.triviaFact: Occupying most of the Iberian Peninsula in southwestern Europe, this country is the world's largest producer of olive oil and holds dozens of distinct regional cultures. Architectural treasures range from the carved Moorish courtyards of the Alhambra in Granada and the Mosque-Cathedral of Córdoba to Antoni Gaudí's towering Sagrada Família church in Barcelona. Passionate flamenco guitar and dance, late-evening tapas dining, and historic festivals like the running of the bulls are part of everyday cultural life.

countries.name: Estonia
countries.triviaFact: Dotted with more than two thousand islands, peat bogs, and thick pine forests along the Baltic Sea, this northern European nation is one of the most digitally advanced societies on Earth. Citizens vote online, sign contracts digitally, and access almost every government service from their phones in minutes. At the same time, its capital preserves a cobblestone medieval Old Town of merchant houses, town walls, and watchtowers that looks straight out of the 15th century.

countries.name: Ethiopia
countries.triviaFact: Rising from the Great Rift Valley into a vast roof of mountains in the Horn of Africa, this is the most populous landlocked country in the world. It was never colonized during the European Scramble for Africa and still uses its own ancient Ge'ez script, a twelve-hour clock cycle starting at dawn, and a thirteen-month calendar. In the northern highlands of Lalibela, medieval builders carved eleven full-sized Christian churches straight down into solid red volcanic rock, and wild Arabica coffee first grew in its southwestern forests.

countries.name: Finland
countries.triviaFact: About 188,000 glacier-carved lakes and endless birch and pine forests cover this Nordic country, where winter brings the Northern Lights and summer brings weeks of midnight sun. Wood-burning and electric saunas are a central part of daily life here, with more than three million saunas for a population of five and a half million people. Consistently ranked as the happiest country in the world, it is also known for its strong public schools and the official hometown of Santa Claus on the Arctic Circle in Rovaniemi.

countries.name: Fiji
countries.triviaFact: More than three hundred volcanic and coral islands make up this South Pacific archipelago, though most people live on the two largest islands. Because the 180th meridian runs directly through the island of Taveuni, you can stand with one foot in the eastern hemisphere and one in the western hemisphere. Visitors are welcomed into villages with a traditional kava root drink ceremony, and the islands are world-famous for soft coral reefs and seven-a-side rugby.

countries.name: Falkland Islands
countries.triviaFact: Two large treeless islands and over seven hundred smaller islets sit in the cold South Atlantic Ocean about five hundred kilometers east of Patagonia. Strong winds sweep across rolling peat moors and white sand beaches where five different species of penguins breed in huge coastal colonies. Sheep outnumber the roughly 3,600 human residents by more than a hundred to one, and the capital features colorful tin-roofed houses and British red phone boxes.

countries.name: France
countries.triviaFact: Shaped roughly like a six-sided hexagon between the Atlantic Ocean, the English Channel, and the Mediterranean Sea, this country is the most visited travel destination in the world. Its capital on the Seine River is home to the Eiffel Tower, the Louvre Museum, and Notre-Dame Cathedral, while royal châteaux line the Loire Valley and snow caps Mont Blanc in the Alps. From Champagne, Bordeaux, and Burgundy wines to hundreds of artisan cheeses and high fashion, its food and art have influenced cultures everywhere.

countries.name: Faroe Islands
countries.triviaFact: Eighteen steep volcanic islands rise out of the stormy North Atlantic midway between Iceland, Norway, and Scotland. There are no native trees across the grassy mountain slopes, where sheep outnumber people and many village houses still wear traditional roofs of living green turf. Engineering teams have bored miles of underwater road tunnels beneath the ocean fjords, including the world's first undersea roundabout, to connect the main islands.

countries.name: Micronesia
countries.triviaFact: More than six hundred tiny islands and coral atolls spread across nearly three thousand kilometers of the western Pacific Ocean to form this federation of four island states. On the rainy volcanic island of Pohnpei stands Nan Madol, a mysterious ancient city of ninety-two artificial islets built from giant basalt stone logs stacked atop a coral reef. Farther west in Yap, villagers historically carved giant donut-shaped stone disks called Rai to use as ceremonial money.

countries.name: Gabon
countries.triviaFact: Thick equatorial rainforests blanket nearly ninety percent of this sparsely populated country on the Atlantic coast of Central Africa. In the early 2000s, the government set aside more than ten percent of the entire national territory into thirteen national parks to protect forest elephants, mandrills, and lowland gorillas. At Loango National Park on the coast, wild hippos, forest elephants, and buffaloes walk right onto the white ocean beaches.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.officialName: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
countries.triviaFact: Made up of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland, this island nation off the northwestern coast of Europe launched the Industrial Revolution in the late 18th century. Its history stretches from the prehistoric stone circle of Stonehenge and Roman baths to medieval castles, Shakespeare's Globe Theatre, and the world's oldest underground subway system. English spoken here became the global language of business and science, while modern sports like football, cricket, rugby, golf, and tennis were all codified on its fields.

countries.name: Georgia
countries.triviaFact: Tucked between the snow-covered peaks of the Greater Caucasus mountains and the Black Sea, this country has one of the oldest winemaking traditions on Earth. Archaeologists found clay jars here showing that locals have fermented grape juice underground in egg-shaped terracotta vessels called qvevri for eight thousand years. Its language has its own curly, thirty-three-letter alphabet found nowhere else, and ancient stone watchtowers still guard high mountain villages in Svaneti.

countries.name: Guernsey
countries.triviaFact: Located in the English Channel closer to the coast of Normandy than to England, this self-governing island bailiwick is a dependency of the British Crown. The famous writer Victor Hugo lived here in exile for fifteen years, writing 'Les Misérables' in a glass-topped lookout room facing the sea. The island is also known for its rich golden-milk dairy cattle, medieval Castle Cornet, and smaller car-free sister islands like Sark and Herm.

countries.name: Ghana
countries.triviaFact: In 1957, under the leadership of Kwame Nkrumah, this coastal West African nation became the first sub-Saharan colony to win independence from European rule. Whitewashed European forts and castles, such as Cape Coast and Elmina, still stand along the Atlantic shore as solemn memorials to the transatlantic slave trade. Inland lies Lake Volta, the largest artificial reservoir in the world by surface area, and master weavers in the Ashanti region hand-loom bright silk and cotton kente cloth.

countries.name: Gibraltar
countries.triviaFact: A massive 426-meter-high wedge of Jurassic limestone juts out from the southern coast of Iberia to guard the narrow strait where the Atlantic Ocean meets the Mediterranean Sea. Over three hundred wild Barbary macaques roam the upper ridge of the peak, making them the only wild monkey population in Europe. Because space is so tight on the six-square-kilometer peninsula, the main road into town crosses directly over the middle of the airport runway.

countries.name: Guinea
countries.triviaFact: High sandstone plateaus in the Fouta Djallon highlands of this West African country catch heavy monsoon rains and feed the sources of the Niger, Senegal, and Gambia rivers. Because three of the region's most important waterways begin here, geographers call the country the Water Tower of West Africa. Beneath its red soil lie the largest reserves of bauxite on the planet, the raw ore used around the world to make aluminum.

countries.name: Guadeloupe
countries.triviaFact: Two main islands separated by a narrow mangrove channel give this French Caribbean archipelago the shape of a giant butterfly. The eastern wing is flat limestone covered in sugarcane fields and white sand beaches, while the western wing rises to the steaming volcanic peak of La Soufrière and dense rainforest waterfalls. As an overseas region of France, it uses the euro and sends representatives to the parliament in Paris.

countries.name: Gambia
countries.triviaFact: Shaped like a crooked finger pointing inland from the Atlantic Ocean, this is the smallest country on the African mainland. Its borders follow the winding banks of its central river for more than three hundred kilometers while never stretching wider than fifty kilometers from north to south. Surrounded on three sides by Senegal, its river wetlands and mangroves attract nearly six hundred species of tropical and migrating birds.

countries.name: Guinea-Bissau
countries.triviaFact: Mangrove swamps and tidal rivers cut deeply into the low coastline of this small West African country. Just offshore lies the Bijagós Archipelago, a labyrinth of eighty-eight islands where sacred traditions have kept the environment nearly untouched. On the island of Orango, rare hippos have adapted to swimming in salty ocean water and resting on sandy sea beaches.

countries.name: Equatorial Guinea
countries.triviaFact: Unlike its neighbors in Central Africa, this is the only sovereign country on the continent where Spanish is an official national language. Its territory is split between a forested mainland region called Río Muni and five volcanic islands out in the Atlantic bight. Strangely, the historic capital Malabo sits on Bioko Island offshore rather than on the larger mainland where most of the population lives.

countries.name: Greece
countries.triviaFact: Sunlit mountains and more than six thousand islands and islets in the Aegean and Ionian seas make up this southern European country. Over two thousand five hundred years ago, its ancient city-states gave birth to democracy, western philosophy, theater, and the Olympic Games. Above the modern capital still stands the marble Parthenon temple on the Acropolis, while whitewashed villages cling to volcanic cliffs on islands like Santorini.

countries.name: Grenada
countries.triviaFact: Fragrant groves of nutmeg, cinnamon, cloves, and cocoa cover the volcanic hills of this southern Caribbean island, earning it the nickname of the Isle of Spice. Every red-and-yellow national flag even features a small drawing of a split nutmeg pod on the left side. Just off the western coast, divers swim through the world's first underwater sculpture park, where stone figures sit on the ocean floor and help new coral reefs grow.

countries.name: Greenland
countries.triviaFact: Stretching between the Arctic and North Atlantic oceans, this autonomous territory of Denmark is the largest non-continental island on Earth. Over eighty percent of its landmass is buried under an ancient ice sheet up to three kilometers thick, leaving only the rocky coastal fjords free for towns. No roads connect any two towns on the entire island, so residents travel everywhere by boat, helicopter, airplane, or dog sled.

countries.name: Guatemala
countries.triviaFact: Steep volcanic cones and highland lakes shape this Central American country, which was the center of the ancient Maya civilization. Deep in the northern Petén jungle, massive limestone temple pyramids at Tikal rise above the rainforest canopy alongside howler monkeys and toucans. Today, nearly half the population descends from Maya groups who weave vibrant hand-loomed textiles and speak more than twenty indigenous languages.

countries.name: French Guiana
countries.triviaFact: Covered almost entirely by dense, unspoiled Amazon rainforest, this overseas department of France sits on the northeastern coast of South America. Because it lies just five degrees north of the equator where Earth's rotation gives rockets an extra boost, the European Space Agency launches its Ariane and Vega satellites from the spaceport at Kourou. Offshore lie the Salvation Islands, including Devil's Island, which France used as a notorious prison colony until the mid-20th century.

countries.name: Guam
countries.triviaFact: Located at the southern end of the Mariana archipelago, this is the largest island in Micronesia and the westernmost territory of the United States. Because it lies just west of the International Date Line, its residents are the first citizens of the country to see the sunrise each morning. Across the island stand prehistoric stone pillars called latte stones, which the indigenous Chamorro people carved to support their houses centuries ago.

countries.name: Guyana
countries.triviaFact: Even though this country sits on the northern mainland of South America, its history, English language, and love of cricket tie it closely to the Caribbean. Dense tropical rainforests cover more than eighty percent of its interior, which is crossed by wide rivers that empty into the Atlantic. Deep in the jungle, the Potaro River plunges 226 meters off a sandstone cliff at Kaieteur Falls, one of the most powerful single-drop waterfalls in the world.

countries.name: Hong Kong
countries.triviaFact: More than five hundred skyscrapers taller than 150 meters pack the harborfront of this special administrative region on China's southern coast, more than any other city on Earth. Double-decker trams and the historic Star Ferry cross between the crowded island and the Kowloon peninsula below Victoria Peak. Despite its famous high-rise density, roughly seventy percent of the territory is actually green mountains, country parks, and outlying islands.

countries.name: Heard Island and McDonald Islands
countries.officialName: Territory of Heard Island and McDonald Islands
countries.triviaFact: Located in the stormy Southern Ocean more than four thousand kilometers southwest of mainland Australia, these subantarctic islands are among the most remote places on Earth. An ice-covered active volcano called Big Ben dominates the main island, and its 2,745-meter summit, Mawson Peak, is actually higher than any mountain on the Australian mainland. No humans live here permanently, leaving the black volcanic beaches entirely to huge colonies of seals and penguins.

countries.name: Honduras
countries.triviaFact: Mountain ranges cover more than three-quarters of this Central American country, which stretches from a long Caribbean coastline to a short shore on the Pacific Gulf of Fonseca. Near the western border stands the ancient Maya city of Copán, famous for its stone portraits of kings and a grand stairway carved with more than two thousand hieroglyphs. Off the northern coast, the Bay Islands sit along the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef and draw divers from around the world.

countries.name: Croatia
countries.triviaFact: More than a thousand rocky islands, reefs, and inlets line the crystal-clear Adriatic coast of this crescent-shaped country. On the southern coast, the medieval walled city of Dubrovnik and the Roman Emperor Diocletian's Palace in Split have stood for centuries. Inland, sixteen blue-green lakes spill into one another over natural limestone dams and waterfalls at Plitvice Lakes National Park.

countries.name: Haiti
countries.triviaFact: Occupying the mountainous western third of the island of Hispaniola, this country made world history on January 1, 1804. After a twelve-year revolution led by Toussaint Louverture and Jean-Jacques Dessalines, formerly enslaved people defeated Napoleon's army to establish the world's first independent Black republic and the second independent nation in the Americas. High on a mountain peak in the north stands the Citadelle Laferrière, the largest stone fortress in the Western Hemisphere.

countries.name: Hungary
countries.triviaFact: Surrounded by the curve of the Carpathian Mountains, this landlocked Central European country sits across the flat fertile plains of the Danube and Tisza rivers. The Danube divides its grand capital into hilly Buda and flat Pest, linked by the historic Chain Bridge beside the Neo-Gothic domes of the Parliament building. Hundreds of natural hot springs bubble up beneath the country, feeding everything from 16th-century Ottoman bathhouses to the large thermal lake at Hévíz.

countries.name: Indonesia
countries.triviaFact: Stretching over five thousand kilometers along the equator between the Indian and Pacific oceans, this is the largest island country in the world, with more than 17,000 islands. Because it sits along the Pacific Ring of Fire, it has over 120 active volcanoes that enrich the soil of densely populated islands like Java and Bali. Its islands shelter the giant Komodo dragon, wild orangutans in Sumatra and Borneo, and the 9th-century Buddhist stupa monument of Borobudur.

countries.name: Isle of Man
countries.triviaFact: Sitting right in the middle of the Irish Sea between Great Britain and Ireland, this self-governing Crown dependency has its own parliament called Tynwald. Founded by Norse Viking settlers in the year 979, Tynwald claims to be the longest continuously operating parliament in the world. Every summer, motorcycle racers speed along its narrow country lanes and stone walls at over 300 kilometers per hour during the famous Tourist Trophy race.

countries.name: India
countries.triviaFact: With more than 1.4 billion citizens speaking dozens of major languages, this South Asian nation is the most populous country and largest democracy in the world. Four major world religions, Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, and Sikhism, began here, alongside mathematical breakthroughs like the number zero and the decimal system. Its landscapes range from the icy peaks of the Himalayas to the white marble domes of the Taj Mahal and the tropical backwaters of the south.

countries.name: British Indian Ocean Territory
countries.triviaFact: Fifty-five low coral islands arranged in seven atolls make up this remote archipelago in the middle of the Indian Ocean, halfway between Africa and Indonesia. The waters surrounding these islands protect one of the largest and healthiest coral reef systems left on the planet. Its largest southern atoll hosts a major joint naval and air base operated by the United Kingdom and the United States, with no permanent civilian residents.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.triviaFact: Mild Atlantic winds and year-round rain keep the pastures of this northwestern European island lush and green all year round. In the Boyne Valley stands Newgrange, a circular stone passage tomb built around 3200 BCE that is older than both Stonehenge and the Egyptian pyramids. The country has produced four Nobel Prize winners in literature, originated Halloween from the ancient Celtic festival of Samhain, and uses a harp as its national symbol.

countries.name: Iran
countries.triviaFact: Sitting between the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf, this mountainous Middle Eastern nation is home to one of the world's oldest continuous civilizations. Ancient kings ruled a vast empire from the carved stone terraces of Persepolis, and medieval builders adorned Isfahan's great square with dazzling turquoise tiles. Desert engineers here invented underground water channels called qanats and tall windcatcher towers that cool homes naturally without electricity.

countries.name: Iraq
countries.triviaFact: Two historic rivers, the Tigris and the Euphrates, flow south from the mountains through this country toward the Persian Gulf, forming a fertile plain where some of the earliest cities in human history began. Starting more than five thousand years ago, the ancient kingdoms of Sumer, Akkad, Babylon, and Assyria arose here and gave humanity cuneiform writing, the wheel, and the first written laws. In the middle ages, its capital became a round walled center of science, medicine, and philosophy during the Islamic Golden Age.

countries.name: Iceland
countries.triviaFact: Positioned just south of the Arctic Circle in the North Atlantic, this island sits directly on the rift where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates pull apart. Erupting geysers, bubbling mud pots, and massive glaciers sit side by side, and underground volcanic heat supplies warm water and clean electricity to nearly every home. Founded at Thingvellir in 930 AD, its national assembly is one of the oldest parliaments in the world, and the country has no standing army or mosquitoes.

countries.name: Israel
countries.triviaFact: Running along the southeastern shore of the Mediterranean Sea, this small Middle Eastern country holds sacred sites for Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. On its eastern border lies the Dead Sea, whose salty shore sits more than four hundred meters below sea level as the lowest exposed land on Earth. Despite having desert across its southern Negev region, the country pioneered drip irrigation and seawater desalination to turn dry land into productive farms.

countries.name: Italy
countries.triviaFact: Shaped like a high-heeled boot kicking the island of Sicily into the Mediterranean Sea, this southern European country holds more UNESCO World Heritage sites than any other nation on Earth. It was the heart of the Roman Empire and the birthplace of the Renaissance in cities like Florence, Venice, and Milan, and it completely surrounds two tiny independent states, Vatican City and San Marino. From pizza, pasta, and espresso to opera and high-speed sports cars, its culture is part of daily life around the globe.

countries.name: Jamaica
countries.triviaFact: Blue mountains rise over two thousand meters above the Caribbean Sea on this lush island, growing some of the world's most sought-after high-altitude coffee beans. Despite a population of under three million people, the island has had a massive impact on global music by giving birth to ska, rocksteady, reggae, and dancehall, led by Bob Marley. Its track and field sprinters also regularly dominate the Olympic Games in the 100-meter and 200-meter dashes.

countries.name: Jersey
countries.triviaFact: Located just twenty-two kilometers off the coast of Normandy, this is the largest and southernmost of the Channel Islands. Although it is a self-governing dependency of the British Crown, many street names and legal customs remain French, and the island experiences some of the largest tidal swings in the world. Every low tide, the ocean pulls back so far that the island nearly doubles in size, revealing rocky reefs and medieval coastal towers.

countries.name: Jordan
countries.triviaFact: Most of this Arab kingdom sits on a high desert plateau east of the Dead Sea and the Great Rift Valley river. Hidden inside a narrow, winding sandstone canyon in the south lies Petra, the ancient capital of the Nabataean kingdom, whose rose-red temples and tombs were carved straight into the cliff walls over two thousand years ago. Farther south, red sand dunes and tall sandstone mountains rise across the desert valley of Wadi Rum.

countries.name: Japan
countries.triviaFact: Four main volcanic islands and thousands of smaller ones curve along the Pacific Ring of Fire to form this East Asian nation. Bullet trains race past the snow-covered cone of Mount Fuji, connecting futuristic neon cities with quiet wooden Shinto shrines, Zen rock gardens, and hot spring inns. Known for having one of the longest life expectancies in the world, the country has shaped global culture through sushi, anime, video games, and robotics.

countries.name: Kazakhstan
countries.triviaFact: Stretching from the Caspian Sea all the way to the Altai Mountains on the Chinese border, this vast Central Asian nation is the largest landlocked country in the world. Endless grassy steppes cover much of the territory, where nomadic horsemen first tamed wild horses thousands of years ago and wild apples first evolved in the southern mountains. Out on the southern steppe sits the Baikonur Cosmodrome, the spaceport from which Sputnik and Yuri Gagarin launched into orbit.

countries.name: Kenya
countries.triviaFact: Bisected by both the equator and the Great Rift Valley, this East African country rises from palm-fringed Indian Ocean beaches to the snow-dusted peak of its namesake mountain. Every year, over a million wildebeest and zebras cross the crocodile-filled Mara River into the Maasai Mara reserve during the Great Migration. The country is also world-famous for its high-altitude distance runners from the Kalenjin community and is the only nation with a wildlife safari park bordering its capital city.

countries.name: Kyrgyzstan
countries.triviaFact: Snow-covered peaks of the Tian Shan mountain range cover more than eighty percent of this landlocked Central Asian country. High in the mountains sits Issyk-Kul, one of the largest and deepest alpine lakes in the world, whose slightly salty waters never freeze even in the middle of winter. Semi-nomadic herders still move their horses and sheep to high summer pastures, sleep in felt yurts, and recite the Epic of Manas, one of the longest poems in human history.

countries.name: Cambodia
countries.triviaFact: Centered on the flat floodplains of the Mekong River and Tonlé Sap lake, this Southeast Asian kingdom was the heart of a powerful medieval empire a thousand years ago. In the northern forests stands Angkor Wat, the largest religious monument ever built, which is so iconic that its towers appear on the national flag. During the annual monsoon, the river flowing out of Tonlé Sap actually reverses direction and expands the lake to more than four times its dry-season size.

countries.name: Kiribati
countries.triviaFact: Thirty-two low-lying coral atolls and one raised coral island lie scattered across 3.5 million square kilometers of the central Pacific Ocean. Because its islands straddle both the equator and the 180th meridian, this is the only country in the world that sits in all four hemispheres at the same time. After realigning the International Date Line in 1995, its eastern Line Islands became the very first inhabited places on Earth to welcome each new day and new year.

countries.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
countries.officialName: Federation of Saint Christopher and Nevis
countries.triviaFact: Two green volcanic islands separated by a three-kilometer channel called The Narrows form the smallest sovereign country in the Western Hemisphere in both area and population. On the larger island, the massive stone walls of Brimstone Hill Fortress, designed by British engineers and built by enslaved Africans, earned the nickname of the Gibraltar of the West Indies. A narrow-gauge railway once built to haul sugarcane from coastal plantations now carries visitors on a scenic loop around the entire main island.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.triviaFact: Sharing a heavily fortified peninsula in East Asia, this country transformed in just a few decades from a war-torn farming society into a global leader in semiconductors, ships, and smartphones. In 1443, King Sejong the Great commissioned scholars to create Hangul, a logical phonetic alphabet designed so that anyone could learn to read and write in a few days. Today, its pop music, films, television dramas, and fermented kimchi dishes are enjoyed by hundreds of millions of fans worldwide.

countries.name: Kosovo
countries.triviaFact: Ringed by the high peaks of the Accursed Mountains and the Šar Mountains, this landlocked Balkan republic declared its independence in February 2008 and has one of the youngest populations in Europe. Four medieval Serbian Orthodox monasteries and churches here, including Visoki Dečani and Gračanica, are recognized by UNESCO for their preserved 14th-century Byzantine frescoes. In the capital, cafés spill onto lively boulevards near the Newborn monument, whose giant letters are repainted with a fresh design every year on independence day.

countries.name: Kuwait
countries.triviaFact: Sitting at the northwestern corner of the Persian Gulf, this small desert country wraps around a wide, shallow bay that served as a natural harbor for centuries. Before oil transformed its economy in the mid-20th century, local sailors built teakwood dhows and dove for pearls across the gulf. Its most famous modern landmark is a trio of slender concrete towers topped with blue-green tiled spheres overlooking the waterfront.

countries.name: Laos
countries.triviaFact: Surrounded by five neighbors in the heart of the Indochinese Peninsula, this mountainous nation is the only landlocked country in Southeast Asia. The mighty Mekong River flows down its western border past gilded Buddhist temples in Luang Prabang and thousands of limestone islands in the south. High on the central Xiangkhoang plateau, thousands of giant prehistoric stone jars sit scattered across the hills from an Iron Age burial culture.

countries.name: Lebanon
countries.triviaFact: Snow-capped mountains rise steeply behind a narrow Mediterranean coastline in this small Middle Eastern country. In ancient times, its coastal cities were the home of the Phoenicians, the master sailors and traders who created the first widely used phonetic alphabet. High in the mountains still grow protected groves of ancient cedar trees, which have been a symbol of the land for thousands of years and appear on the national flag.

countries.name: Liberia
countries.triviaFact: Founded in 1822 as a settlement for freed African Americans, this West African nation declared its independence in 1847 and is the oldest modern republic on the continent. Its capital was named in honor of James Monroe, the fifth president of the United States, who supported the settlement effort. Dense tropical rainforests cover much of the interior and shelter rare pygmy hippos and forest chimpanzees.

countries.name: Libya
countries.triviaFact: More than ninety percent of this large North African country is covered by the dry plains and sand seas of the Sahara Desert. Along its long Mediterranean coastline stand some of the largest and best-preserved Roman cities in the world, including Leptis Magna and Sabratha. Beneath the southern desert sands, a massive network of underground pipes carries fossil water pumped from ancient aquifers to coastal cities.

countries.name: Saint Lucia
countries.triviaFact: Two dramatic cone-shaped volcanic peaks called the Pitons rise nearly eight hundred meters straight out of the Caribbean Sea on this island's southwestern coast. Visitors can also drive right into the steaming crater of Sulphur Springs, where mud pools bubble inside a collapsed volcanic caldera. This small island has produced two Nobel Prize laureates, giving it the highest number of Nobel winners per person of any sovereign country.

countries.name: Liechtenstein
countries.triviaFact: Wedged between Switzerland and Austria in the upper Rhine Valley, this tiny Alpine principality is one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world. It measures just twenty-five kilometers from north to south, has no airport of its own, and uses the Swiss franc as its currency. Despite its small size, it is a major industrial hub that makes more false teeth and precision power tools than almost anywhere else.

countries.name: Sri Lanka
countries.officialName: Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka
countries.triviaFact: Shaped like a teardrop off the southern tip of India, this tropical island nation rises from palm-lined beaches to misty central mountains covered in tea estates. Rising two hundred meters above the northern jungle is Sigiriya, a 5th-century royal palace built on top of a giant flat-topped rock column with painted frescoes on its walls. The island is also famous for cinnamon, blue sapphires, large herds of wild Asian elephants, and the sacred Temple of the Tooth in Kandy.

countries.name: Lesotho
countries.triviaFact: Completely surrounded on all sides by South Africa, this mountainous kingdom is one of only three enclaved countries in the world. It is the only independent nation on Earth where every single square meter of land sits more than 1,000 meters above sea level. Herders in the high mountains wear thick patterned wool blankets and ride hardy Basotho ponies across snow-dusted passes in winter.

countries.name: Lithuania
countries.triviaFact: Located at the southern end of the Baltic trio, this country was once the center of a medieval grand duchy that stretched all the way from the Baltic Sea to the Black Sea. Its language is the oldest surviving Indo-European tongue in everyday use and preserves grammar patterns strikingly close to ancient Sanskrit. Just west of the capital stands Trakai Castle on an island in a lake, while northern pilgrims have left hundreds of thousands of wooden crosses on a small mound called the Hill of Crosses.

countries.name: Luxembourg
countries.triviaFact: Tucked between Belgium, France, and Germany, this small Western European nation is the last remaining sovereign grand duchy in the world. Its capital city sits perched on dramatic sandstone cliffs cut by deep river gorges and features miles of underground defense tunnels called the Bock Casemates. In 2020, it became the first country in the world to make all public buses, trams, and trains completely free for everyone nationwide.

countries.name: Latvia
countries.triviaFact: Dense pine forests cover more than half of this Baltic nation, and its wide sandy beaches stretch for five hundred kilometers along the sea. Its historic capital sits at the mouth of the Daugava River and contains the largest collection of ornate Art Nouveau buildings in the world. In the western town of Kuldīga, the Venta River spills over a brick-wide limestone ledge to form the widest natural waterfall in Europe.

countries.name: Macau
countries.triviaFact: Connected to southern China on the western side of the Pearl River Delta, this tiny peninsula and two joined islands served as a Portuguese trading post for more than four hundred years until 1999. Cobblestone plazas and pastel churches like the ruined stone facade of Saint Paul stand right next to traditional Chinese temples. Today, it is the most densely populated region in the world and generates more revenue from resort casinos than any other city.

countries.name: Saint Martin
countries.triviaFact: Since the signing of the Treaty of Concordia in 1648, this small Caribbean island has been peacefully divided between France in the north and the Netherlands in the south. People drive freely across the open border between the two halves without any passport checks or customs gates. The northern French collectivity is known for its open-air waterfront markets in Marigot, hillside nature trails, and gourmet bistros.

countries.name: Morocco
countries.triviaFact: Stretching from the Mediterranean Sea and the Atlantic Ocean across the snow-capped Atlas Mountains into the Sahara, this North African kingdom sits just fourteen kilometers south of Europe. Founded in the year 859 by Fatima al-Fihri in the walled city of Fez, the University of al-Qarawiyyin is recognized as the oldest continuously operating university in the world. Visitors wander through colorful souks, the blue-painted mountain alleys of Chefchaouen, and bustling night food stalls in Marrakech.

countries.name: Monaco
countries.triviaFact: Covering just over two square kilometers along the French Riviera, this tiny Mediterranean principality is the second-smallest independent state in the world and the most densely populated. With no personal income tax, its yacht-filled harbor at Monte Carlo attracts wealthy residents from around the globe. Every spring, Formula One race cars roar through its narrow city streets, tight hairpin turns, and waterfront tunnel during one of the world's most famous motor races.

countries.name: Moldova
countries.triviaFact: Wedged between Romania and Ukraine along the Dniester and Prut rivers, this landlocked Eastern European country has rich black soil ideal for growing grapes and sunflowers. Beneath the hills near the capital lies Mileștii Mici, an underground limestone tunnel network that holds nearly two million bottles of wine and is the largest wine cellar in the world. Monks also carved the medieval cave monastery of Orheiul Vechi high into a curved limestone cliff above the Răut River.

countries.name: Madagascar
countries.triviaFact: Separated from the African mainland for roughly eighty-eight million years, the world's fourth-largest island evolved its own unique world of plants and animals. More than ninety percent of its wildlife, including over a hundred species of lemurs, fossas, and giant baobab trees, lives nowhere else on Earth. Small farmers in the humid northeast also hand-pollinate orchids to grow roughly eighty percent of the world's natural vanilla beans.

countries.name: Maldives
countries.triviaFact: Nearly 1,200 tiny coral islands grouped into twenty-six ring-shaped atolls form this Indian Ocean nation southwest of India. With an average ground level of just one and a half meters above the waves and a highest natural point under three meters, it is the flattest and lowest-lying country on the planet. Crystal-clear lagoons and coral walls make fishing and overwater resort tourism the backbone of the economy.

countries.name: Mexico
countries.triviaFact: Bridging North and Central America, this country has the largest number of Spanish speakers in the world and was the home of the Olmec, Maya, Zapotec, and Aztec civilizations. Ancient farmers here first domesticated corn, tomatoes, avocados, chili peppers, and cacao, giving the world chocolate and one of its richest culinary traditions. Famous sights include the stepped pyramid of Chichén Itzá, natural limestone sinkholes called cenotes, and mountain forests where millions of monarch butterflies spend the winter.

countries.name: Marshall Islands
countries.triviaFact: Twenty-nine coral atolls and five isolated islands form two parallel chains known as the Sunrise and Sunset chains across the central Pacific Ocean. For centuries, master island navigators sailed between tiny low-lying atolls out of sight of land using woven palm-stick charts that mapped how islands bend ocean wave swells. After World War II, Bikini and Enewetak atolls in the north were used for major nuclear testing, and Bikini's sunken fleet is now a UNESCO World Heritage site.

countries.name: North Macedonia
countries.triviaFact: Mountains and deep valleys frame this landlocked Balkan country, which sits along the Vardar River north of Greece. On its southwestern border lies Lake Ohrid, one of Europe's oldest and deepest lakes, which has been continuously inhabited for thousands of years and shelters two hundred endemic species. In the 9th century, Saint Clement established a famous medieval school on the lakeshore that helped spread the Cyrillic script across the Slavic world.

countries.name: Mali
countries.triviaFact: Stretching from the Niger River valley into the southern Sahara, this landlocked West African country was the heart of powerful medieval empires that grew rich trading gold and salt. In the 14th century, its emperor Mansa Musa was so wealthy that his pilgrimage to Mecca flooded Mediterranean markets with gold, and Timbuktu became a world center of Islamic scholarship with hundreds of thousands of manuscripts. Farther south on the Bani River stands the Great Mosque of Djenné, the largest mud-brick building in the world, which locals replaster by hand every spring.

countries.name: Malta
countries.triviaFact: Sitting in the center of the Mediterranean Sea south of Sicily, this small archipelago has one of the highest population densities in Europe. Prehistoric islanders built massive freestanding limestone temples here, such as Ġgantija and Ħaġar Qim, around 3600 BCE, making them older than both Stonehenge and the Egyptian pyramids. Later, the Knights of Saint John fortified the Grand Harbour with golden limestone bastions and built the walled capital city.

countries.name: Myanmar
countries.officialName: Republic of the Union of Myanmar
countries.triviaFact: Golden Buddhist stupas gleam across the hills and river plains of this Southeast Asian country, which stretches from the Himalayas down to the Andaman Sea. On the dry central plains of Bagan along the Irrawaddy River, more than two thousand red-brick temples and pagodas built between the 11th and 13th centuries still rise above the trees. In the south stands the 99-meter-tall Shwedagon Pagoda, covered in thousands of gold plates and encrusted with diamonds and rubies at its tip.

countries.name: Montenegro
countries.triviaFact: Roughly the size of Connecticut, this Balkan country packs jagged limestone peaks, glacial lakes, and a sunny Adriatic coastline into a compact space. On the coast, the submerged river canyon of the Bay of Kotor winds nearly thirty kilometers inland beneath sheer mountain walls and medieval stone towns. Inland, the turquoise Tara River carves a 1,300-meter-deep gorge through Durmitor National Park, making it the deepest river canyon in Europe.

countries.name: Mongolia
countries.triviaFact: Wedged between Russia and China across high steppes and the Gobi Desert, this is the most sparsely populated independent country in the world. In the 13th century, Genghis Khan united its nomadic horse tribes to build the largest contiguous land empire in human history. Today, nearly a third of the population still lives as nomadic herders moving felt gers across pastures under a sky that stays cloudless for more than 250 days a year.

countries.name: Northern Mariana Islands
countries.officialName: Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands
countries.triviaFact: Fourteen volcanic and coral islands curve north from Guam in the western Pacific to form this United States commonwealth. Just east of the islands, the ocean floor plunges into the deepest ocean trench on Earth at nearly eleven kilometers below the surface. White beaches and clear lagoons on the main island of Saipan sit alongside rusty tanks, bunkers, and cliffside memorials from major World War II battles.

countries.name: Mozambique
countries.triviaFact: Stretching for 2,500 kilometers along the southeastern coast of Africa, this country looks out across the warm waters of the Indian Ocean toward Madagascar. Offshore coral islands in the Bazaruto and Quirimbas archipelagos shelter rare marine dugongs, whale sharks, and sea turtles, while wooden dhows with triangular sails still carry local cargo. After years of recovery, Gorongosa National Park in the central rift valley has become one of Africa's greatest wildlife restoration stories.

countries.name: Mauritania
countries.triviaFact: Almost ninety percent of this large Northwest African country lies within the Sahara Desert, where nomadic Moorish communities have herded camels and traded across oasis towns like Chinguetti for centuries. Out in the central desert plateau sits the Richat Structure, a giant circular bullseye of concentric rock rings fifty kilometers wide that astronauts use as a landmark from space. Every day, one of the longest and heaviest freight trains in the world rumbles for 700 kilometers across the desert to carry iron ore to the Atlantic coast.

countries.name: Montserrat
countries.triviaFact: Thick green forests and strong Irish heritage from 17th-century settlers shaped the culture of this small British territory in the eastern Caribbean. It is the only place outside Ireland that celebrates Saint Patrick's Day as a week-long public holiday, and its passport stamp is a green shamrock. After the Soufrière Hills volcano began erupting in 1995 and buried the southern capital of Plymouth in ash and mud, residents built a new town in the safe northern hills.

countries.name: Martinique
countries.triviaFact: Dominated by the active volcanic peak of Mount Pelée in the eastern Caribbean, this island is an overseas department and region of France. In 1902, a devastating eruption of Mount Pelée destroyed the old coastal town of Saint-Pierre, once known as the Paris of the Caribbean, in just a few minutes. Today, the island is famous for its black-sand northern beaches, botanical gardens, and French-protected agricultural rum distilled from fresh-pressed sugarcane juice.

countries.name: Mauritius
countries.triviaFact: Ringed by coral reefs in the Indian Ocean east of Madagascar, this volcanic island was the only home of the flightless dodo bird before sailors drove it to extinction in the 1600s. Its people blend Indian, African, French, and Chinese heritage into a peaceful society famous for sega music and street foods like dholl puri. At the southwestern tip of the island, sand and silt flowing down an ocean drop-off create the breathtaking optical illusion of a giant underwater waterfall.

countries.name: Malawi
countries.triviaFact: Running down a narrow valley in southeastern Africa, this landlocked country is dominated by a giant crystal-clear rift lake that covers nearly a third of its total area. That lake holds more species of colorful cichlid fish than any other lake on the planet, making it a UNESCO World Heritage site. Known across the continent for its friendly villages, the country exports large harvests of tea and tobacco grown in its southern highlands.

countries.name: Malaysia
countries.triviaFact: Split by the South China Sea into a busy peninsula and the northern third of the island of Borneo, this Southeast Asian country blends diverse Asian and indigenous Borneo cultures. In the capital stand the 88-story twin Petronas Towers, the tallest twin skyscrapers in the world, while Taman Negara protects a tropical rainforest that is 130 million years old. Across the sea on Borneo, Mount Kinabalu rises over four thousand meters above jungles that shelter wild orangutans and giant Rafflesia flowers.

countries.name: Mayotte
