countries.triviaFact: Situated at the northern entrance to the Mozambique Channel between Madagascar and mainland Africa, this volcanic island group is the poorest and newest overseas department of France. A giant coral barrier reef circles the entire territory, enclosing one of the largest and deepest protected tropical lagoons in the world. Every winter, humpback whales swim into the calm lagoon waters to give birth, while brown lemurs leap through the coastal mango and ylang-ylang trees.

countries.name: Namibia
countries.triviaFact: Running along the southwestern coast of Africa, this sparsely populated country takes its name from the coastal desert that geologists consider the oldest desert on Earth. At Sossusvlei, rusty-red sand dunes over three hundred meters high tower above white clay pans dotted with nine-hundred-year-old blackened camelthorn trees. Along the foggy Skeleton Coast, cold Atlantic currents cause thick mist that has wrecked hundreds of ships onto the desert beach over the centuries.

countries.name: New Caledonia
countries.triviaFact: Located in the southwest Pacific about 1,200 kilometers east of Australia, this French special collectivity consists of a long mountainous main island and the coral Loyalty Islands. A continuous 1,500-kilometer barrier reef surrounds the islands, creating the world's largest coral lagoon. Its red soil holds roughly a quarter of the world's nickel reserves and supports ancient cone-shaped pine trees that have survived since the age of dinosaurs.

countries.name: Niger
countries.triviaFact: Named after the great river that flows across its southwestern corner, this is the largest landlocked country in West Africa, with more than four-fifths of its territory covered by the Sahara. In the historic desert crossroads town of Agadez stands a 16th-century mud-brick mosque tower bristling with wooden support beams. Deep in the remote Tenere desert sands, paleontologists have unearthed complete skeletons of giant crocodile-like predators and long-necked dinosaurs.

countries.name: Norfolk Island
countries.triviaFact: Tall native pine trees cover the rolling green hills and steep sea cliffs of this tiny Australian external territory in the South Pacific. Britain first used the isolated island as a harsh penal colony in the late 18th and early 19th centuries, leaving behind Georgian stone ruins at Kingston. In 1856, the British government resettled the entire population of Pitcairn Island, descendants of the HMS Bounty mutineers and Tahitian women, here when they outgrew their tiny home.

countries.name: Nigeria
countries.triviaFact: With more than 220 million residents and over five hundred spoken languages, this West African nation is the most populous country in Africa and has one of the largest youth populations on Earth. Its commercial hub of Lagos drives the global boom in Afrobeats music and Nollywood, which produces more films each year than Hollywood. From the ancient bronze sculptures of Benin City and the walled dye pits of Kano to the oil-rich delta of the south, it is the largest economy in West Africa.

countries.name: Nicaragua
countries.triviaFact: Stretching from the Pacific Ocean to the Caribbean Sea, this is the largest country by land area in Central America. Its massive inland freshwater lake wraps around Ometepe, an island formed by two tall volcanic cones, and is one of the few freshwater lakes in the world inhabited by ocean bull sharks. Visitors also hike up the black volcanic gravel of Cerro Negro near the colonial city of León to slide down the active volcano's slope on wooden boards.

countries.name: Niue
countries.triviaFact: Instead of a chain of low sandy islands, this self-governing South Pacific nation is a single massive raised coral atoll whose limestone cliffs drop straight into deep ocean water. Fewer than two thousand people live on the island itself, while more than ten times as many citizens live and work in New Zealand. In 2020, it became the first entire country in the world to be officially recognized as an International Dark Sky Place for stargazing.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.triviaFact: Roughly a quarter of this flat northwestern European country actually sits below sea level, reclaimed from the sea over centuries using dikes, canals, and windmills. Its main commercial port at Rotterdam is the largest seaport in Europe, while the International Court of Justice sits in The Hague. Famous for cycling paths where bikes outnumber people, golden-age painters like Rembrandt and Van Gogh, and vast fields of spring tulips, it is also the world's second-largest exporter of agricultural goods by value.

countries.name: Norway
countries.triviaFact: Deep glacier-carved fjords, thousands of coastal islands, and high mountain plateaus stretch along the western edge of the Scandinavian Peninsula into the Arctic Circle. A thousand years ago, Viking sailors set out from these shores in wooden longships and left behind ornate all-wood stave churches that still stand today. Powered almost entirely by clean hydroelectricity and backed by the world's largest sovereign wealth fund, the country also runs the Global Seed Vault in the Arctic and awards the Nobel Peace Prize.

countries.name: Nepal
countries.triviaFact: Wedged between China and India along the southern slopes of the Himalayas, this country contains eight of the world's ten highest mountain peaks, including Mount Everest at 8,848 meters. In the southern plains of Lumbini lies the historic birthplace of Siddhartha Gautama, the founder of Buddhism, while medieval brick pagoda temples fill the valleys around the capital. It is the only country in the world whose national flag is not a rectangle or square, shaped instead like two stacked crimson pennants.

countries.name: Nauru
countries.triviaFact: Covering just twenty-one square kilometers in the central Pacific south of the equator, this single oval coral island is the smallest independent republic in the world. For decades in the 20th century, mining the thick layer of bird-droppings phosphate rock that covered its central plateau briefly gave its small population one of the highest incomes per person on Earth. A single 19-kilometer coastal road loops all the way around the flat sandy fringe where nearly all residents live.

countries.name: New Zealand
aliases: Land of the Long White Cloud
countries.triviaFact: Two large islands and hundreds of smaller ones in the southwestern Pacific make up one of the last major landmasses on Earth to be settled by humans, when Polynesian navigators arrived around seven hundred years ago. Because it split from ancient Gondwana without land mammals, flightless birds like the nocturnal kiwi and giant extinct moa evolved to fill the forests. Its landscapes pack steaming geysers in Rotorua, active volcanoes, and the sheer granite fjords of Milford Sound into a country famous for Māori haka dances and rugby.

countries.name: Oman
countries.triviaFact: Guarding the mouth of the Persian Gulf at the southeastern corner of the Arabian Peninsula, this sultanate has the oldest independent state history in the Arab world. Unlike its high-rise neighbors, strict building codes keep cities low-rise and whitewashed, while ancient mud-brick forts like Bahla and Nizwa guard mountain oases watered by historic falaj channels. In the southern region of Dhofar, summer monsoon mists turn the coastal mountains green and nourish the wild trees that produce precious frankincense resin.

countries.name: Pakistan
countries.triviaFact: Stretching from the Arabian Sea along the fertile Indus River plain up to the icy junction of the Himalaya, Karakoram, and Hindu Kush ranges, this is the fifth most populous country in the world. Over four thousand years ago, the Indus Valley Civilization built planned brick cities with indoor plumbing here at Mohenjo-daro and Harappa. Its northern mountains contain K2, the second-highest peak on Earth, more glacial ice than anywhere outside the polar regions, and artisans in Sialkot hand-stitch most of the world's professional footballs.

countries.name: Panama
countries.triviaFact: Forming the narrow S-shaped land bridge that connects Central and South America, this country is famous for the 82-kilometer canal that lifts giant cargo ships over the continental divide between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans. Because the isthmus twists from west to east, its capital is the only place in the world where you can watch the sun rise over the Pacific Ocean and set over the Atlantic. Dense tropical jungles bordering the canal zone harbor nearly a thousand species of birds, more than all of North America north of Mexico.

countries.name: Pitcairn Islands
countries.officialName: Pitcairn, Henderson, Ducie and Oeno Islands
countries.triviaFact: With only around forty to fifty permanent residents living in the single village of Adamstown, this tiny volcanic rock in the South Pacific is the least populated jurisdiction in the world. In 1790, nine mutineers from the British ship HMS Bounty and their Tahitian companions burned their ship in Bounty Bay here to hide from the Royal Navy. With no airstrip or safe harbor, supplies arrive only a few times a year by cargo ship and must be ferried ashore through crashing surf in open longboats.

countries.name: Peru
countries.triviaFact: Rising from a dry Pacific coastal strip to the snow-capped Andes and the headwaters of the Amazon River, this South American country was the center of the Inca Empire and earlier Norte Chico civilization. High on a misty mountain ridge above the Urubamba Valley stands the 15th-century stone citadel of Machu Picchu, while giant ancient animal figures called the Nazca Lines lie etched into the southern desert floor. Highland farmers here first domesticated the potato thousands of years ago and still grow more than three thousand varieties.

countries.name: Philippines
countries.triviaFact: More than 7,600 tropical islands form this western Pacific archipelago, which is divided into the three main regions of Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. Two thousand years ago, indigenous Ifugao farmers carved giant stepped rice terraces by hand into the steep mountains of northern Luzon, while underground rivers wind through limestone caves in Palawan and over a thousand cone-shaped Chocolate Hills dot Bohol. Colorful jeepneys originally built from left-behind World War II military jeeps remain the most iconic form of public transport across the islands.

countries.name: Palau
countries.triviaFact: More than three hundred emerald-green limestone Rock Islands shaped like giant mushrooms float in a turquoise lagoon across this western Pacific archipelago. In 2009, the country created the world's first national shark sanctuary, banning all commercial shark fishing across an ocean zone the size of France, and visitors must sign an eco-pledge stamped directly into their passports upon arrival. Historically, many traditional clans followed a matrilineal system in which women chose the village chiefs and controlled family land and money.

countries.name: Papua New Guinea
countries.officialName: Independent State of Papua New Guinea
countries.triviaFact: Occupying the eastern half of the world's second-largest island along with hundreds of offshore islands, this country is the most linguistically diverse place on Earth. Steep mountains and dense rainforest valleys kept tribes so isolated for thousands of years that citizens speak more than 840 distinct living languages, roughly twelve percent of all languages in the world. Its highland valleys were one of the earliest places on Earth where people independently developed farming seven thousand years ago, and its forests shelter colorful birds-of-paradise and tree kangaroos.

countries.name: Poland
countries.triviaFact: Stretching from the sandy shores of the Baltic Sea to the granite peaks of the Tatra Mountains in Central Europe, this country has rebuilt itself repeatedly across centuries of turbulent history. After its capital was almost completely leveled during World War II, citizens used 18th-century canaletto paintings to reconstruct the colorful Old Town brick by brick. In the south lies the medieval royal city of Kraków and the Wieliczka Salt Mine, where miners carved underground chapels, statues, and chandeliers entirely out of gray rock salt.

countries.name: Puerto Rico
countries.triviaFact: Situated at the eastern end of the Greater Antilles, this self-governing Caribbean archipelago is an unincorporated territory of the United States where Spanish and English are both official languages. Five hundred years of Spanish colonial history remain visible in the blue cobblestone streets and massive stone sea forts of El Morro and San Cristóbal guarding the old harbor. Inland rises El Yunque, the only tropical rainforest in the United States National Forest System, while three coastal bays glow blue at night with microscopic bioluminescent organisms.

countries.name: North Korea
countries.triviaFact: Occupying the northern half of a divided East Asian peninsula between the Yellow Sea and the Sea of Japan, this mountainous state has been separated from its southern neighbor by a four-kilometer-wide Demilitarized Zone since 1953. Sacred Mount Paektu, an active volcano with a deep crater lake on the northern border, holds a central place in local folklore, while the jagged granite peaks of the Diamond Mountains rise in the southeast. The country uses its own Juche calendar system that counts years starting from 1912, the birth year of founder Kim Il Sung.

countries.name: Portugal
countries.triviaFact: Facing the Atlantic Ocean along the western edge of the Iberian Peninsula, this country has kept almost the exact same mainland borders since the 13th century, making it one of the oldest nation-states in Europe. During the 15th and 16th centuries, its navigators pioneered sea routes around Africa to India and across to Brazil, leaving behind ornate maritime monuments like the Tower of Belém. Today, it is famous for blue-and-white azulejo ceramic tiles, soulful Fado singing, port wine from the Douro Valley, and producing over half of the world's cork.

countries.name: Paraguay
countries.triviaFact: Bisected by the wide river that gives this landlocked South American country its name, it splits into fertile red-soil hills in the east and the vast, dry thorny scrubland of the Gran Chaco in the west. Unlike almost any other country in the Americas, an indigenous language, Guaraní, is spoken by the vast majority of the non-indigenous population alongside Spanish and appears on the national currency. On its borders, the massive Itaipu and Yacyretá hydroelectric dams generate so much clean electricity that the country is one of the largest net exporters of clean power in the world.

countries.name: Palestine
countries.triviaFact: Split between the hilly West Bank along the Jordan River and the coastal Gaza Strip on the Mediterranean Sea, this land sits at the heart of the ancient Levant. In the Jordan Valley lies Jericho, an oasis town more than ten thousand years old that archaeologists recognize as one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities on Earth. Terraced hills planted with centuries-old olive trees surround historic towns like Bethlehem, Hebron, and Nablus, where artisans still make traditional olive-oil soap and hand-stitched tatreez embroidery.

countries.name: French Polynesia
countries.triviaFact: One hundred and eighteen volcanic islands and coral atolls lie scattered across an ocean area the size of Western Europe in the South Pacific. Lush green peaks rise out of turquoise lagoons on famous islands like Moorea and Bora Bora, where overwater bungalows were first invented for travelers. The English word 'tattoo' comes directly from the indigenous local word 'tatau', a sacred body-marking art practiced across these islands for centuries.

countries.name: Qatar
countries.triviaFact: Jutting northward into the Persian Gulf from the Arabian Peninsula, this small desert thumb of land holds the world's third-largest reserves of natural gas, giving its residents one of the highest incomes per person on Earth. Before oil and gas, its coastal towns were quiet pearling villages, and traditional wooden dhows still float in the harbor opposite the futuristic glass skyscrapers of West Bay. In 2022, it became the first Arab and Middle Eastern country to host the FIFA World Cup, alongside landmarks like the Museum of Islamic Art.

countries.name: Réunion
countries.triviaFact: Rising steeply out of the Indian Ocean between Madagascar and Mauritius, this volcanic island is an overseas department and region of France. Its interior is carved into three huge collapsed volcanic amphitheaters called cirques that can only be reached by winding mountain roads or helicopter, alongside Piton de la Fournaise, one of the world's most active volcanoes. Because of its steep microclimates, the island holds world records for the heaviest rainfall ever measured in twelve, twenty-four, and seventy-two hours.

countries.name: Romania
countries.triviaFact: Curving through the middle of this southeastern European country, the forested Carpathian Mountains encircle the historic plateau of Transylvania and shelter Europe's largest populations of brown bears and wolves. Medieval Saxon settlers built fortified churches and hilltop castles like Bran Castle, popularly linked to the Dracula legend, while northern monasteries in Bucovina feature vivid 16th-century frescoes painted on their outer walls. Where the Danube River meets the Black Sea in the east, it fans out into Europe's largest and best-preserved river delta wetland.

countries.name: Russia
countries.triviaFact: Stretching across northern Eurasia from the Baltic Sea all the way to the Pacific Ocean, this is the largest country in the world by a wide margin, covering eleven time zones and more than a ninth of Earth's land area. Its vast Siberian wilderness holds the world's largest forest belt and Lake Baikal, which is the deepest and oldest freshwater lake on the planet and contains twenty percent of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water. From the colorful onion domes of Saint Basil's Cathedral on Red Square and the Hermitage Museum to launching the first satellite and human into space, its history spans empires and continents.

countries.name: Rwanda
countries.triviaFact: Dotted with green rolling hills, this high-altitude, landlocked country in the Great Rift Valley is one of the most densely populated nations on the African mainland. In the misty bamboo forests of the Virunga volcanoes in the northwest, conservationists protect a growing population of endangered mountain gorillas first studied by Dian Fossey. On the last Saturday of every month, businesses close and citizens across the country join in Umuganda, a morning of community cleanup that has made its capital one of the cleanest cities in Africa, and women hold over sixty percent of seats in its parliament.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
countries.triviaFact: Covering roughly four-fifths of a vast desert peninsula between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf, this kingdom is the birthplace of Islam and custodian of its two holiest mosques in Mecca and Medina. In the south lies the Rub' al Khali, or Empty Quarter, the largest continuous sand desert in the world, while the northwest preserves the 2,000-year-old carved sandstone tombs of Hegra. Having no permanent natural rivers anywhere in the country, it relies on underground aquifers and leads the world in producing fresh drinking water from desalinated seawater.

countries.name: Sudan
countries.triviaFact: In the central capital of this large northeastern African country, the White Nile and the Blue Nile merge together before flowing north through the Sahara toward the Mediterranean. Although Egypt is more famous for pyramids, the ancient Kingdom of Kush actually built more than two hundred steep-sided stone pyramids here at Meroë, El Kurru, and Nuri, nearly twice as many as stand in Egypt. Its landscapes range from Red Sea coral reefs in the east to vast dry savannas and desert plains.

countries.name: Senegal
countries.triviaFact: Located at the westernmost point of the African mainland where the Sahel meets the Atlantic Ocean, this country wraps around the narrow river enclave of The Gambia. Just off the tip of the capital peninsula sits Gorée Island, whose pastel colonial houses and House of Slaves serve as a UNESCO World Heritage memorial to the transatlantic slave trade. Near the coast lies Lake Retba, a shallow lagoon whose high salt levels and harmless algae turn the water a bright strawberry pink under the dry-season sun.

countries.name: Singapore
countries.triviaFact: Connected by bridges to the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula, this diamond-shaped island and sixty smaller islets form one of the only surviving sovereign city-states in the world. Over the past sixty years, land reclamation and trade turned a small port without natural resources into a global hub for shipping, finance, and aviation, featuring the indoor waterfall at Changi Airport and the solar-powered Supertrees of Gardens by the Bay. It is also the only country whose national anthem is printed in micro-text on the back of its thousand-dollar note, and its open-air hawker food centers are recognized by UNESCO.

countries.name: South Georgia
countries.officialName: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
countries.triviaFact: Snow-covered mountains and massive glaciers rise directly out of the icy South Atlantic Ocean across this remote subantarctic territory. No permanent residents live here today, though rusted boilers and wooden buildings remain from early 20th-century whaling stations like Grytviken, where polar explorer Sir Ernest Shackleton is buried. Every summer, the beaches are packed shoulder to shoulder with millions of fur seals, giant elephant seals, and over four hundred thousand breeding pairs of king penguins.

countries.name: Svalbard and Jan Mayen
countries.triviaFact: Situated halfway between mainland Norway and the North Pole, this Arctic archipelago experiences four months of continuous midnight sun in summer and four months of polar darkness in winter. Polar bears outnumber the roughly 2,500 residents on the main island, and carved deep inside a frozen sandstone mountain near the main town sits the Global Seed Vault, which safeguards backup copies of over a million crop seeds from around the world. Farther south in the North Atlantic lies a lonely volcanic island topped by the northernmost active volcano on Earth above sea level.

countries.name: Solomon Islands
countries.triviaFact: Nearly a thousand volcanic islands and coral atolls stretch across the southwestern Pacific Ocean east of Papua New Guinea. During World War II, the fiercest land and naval battles of the Pacific campaign took place here on Guadalcanal, leaving dozens of warships and planes sunken in the waters of Ironbottom Sound. Today, the archipelago is known for Marovo Lagoon, the largest double-barrier reef lagoon in the world, and for coastal villagers who dive on a single breath to hunt fish.

countries.name: Sierra Leone
countries.triviaFact: Ringed by white sand beaches and green coastal mountains that 15th-century Portuguese sailors named after roaring lions, this West African nation has one of the largest natural harbors in the world. Its capital was founded in 1792 as a home for formerly enslaved people from North America, Jamaica, and rescued slave ships, who developed the widely spoken Krio language. Alluvial rivers in the eastern interior have produced some of the largest gem-quality diamonds ever found.

countries.name: El Salvador
countries.triviaFact: Facing the Pacific Ocean without a Caribbean coast, this is the smallest and most densely populated country in Central America. More than twenty volcanoes, including the steep cone of Izalco, once called the Lighthouse of the Pacific by sailors because of its constant glow, rise across its green interior. Thick corn tortillas stuffed with cheese, beans, and pork called pupusas are the beloved national dish, and long right-hand ocean swells draw surfers from around the world.

countries.name: San Marino
countries.triviaFact: Perched high on the three rocky limestone peaks of Mount Titano and completely surrounded by Italy, this tiny microstate claims to be the oldest surviving sovereign republic in the world. According to tradition, a Christian stonemason founded a free community on the mountain in 301 AD to escape Roman persecution, and its 1600 AD written constitution is the oldest still in effect. Instead of a single president, two co-equal Captains Regent are elected every six months to serve together as heads of state.

countries.name: Somalia
countries.triviaFact: Shaped like the number seven along the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean, this Horn of Africa nation has the longest coastline on the African mainland at more than 3,000 kilometers. In the northern hills of Laas Geel, rock shelters preserve remarkably vivid 5,000-year-old cave paintings of long-horned cattle and herders that still look freshly painted. Famous in ancient times for exporting aromatic myrrh and frankincense resin to pharaohs, the country also has a rich oral tradition of poetry and holds the largest camel population in the world.

countries.name: Saint Pierre and Miquelon
countries.officialName: Overseas Collectivity of Saint-Pierre and Miquelon
countries.triviaFact: Located just twenty-five kilometers off the southern coast of Newfoundland in Canada, this small group of rocky islands is the last remaining piece of the colonial territory of New France in North America. Although it sits in Canadian waters, it is an overseas collectivity of France where residents use the euro, buy fresh baguettes, and drive cars with French license plates under subarctic Atlantic fogs. During the 1920s Prohibition era in the United States, the islands briefly boomed as a legal warehouse port for shipping whiskey south.

countries.name: Serbia
countries.triviaFact: Centered where the Danube and Sava rivers meet below the ancient stone walls of Kalemegdan Fortress, this landlocked Balkan country links Central and Southeastern Europe. Over the centuries, eighteen Roman emperors, including Constantine the Great, were born within its modern borders, and medieval kings built painted Orthodox monasteries like Studenica in the southern valleys. Today, the country is one of the world's top exporters of raspberries, a global leader in basketball, water polo, and tennis, and the ancestral homeland of electrical pioneer Nikola Tesla.

countries.name: South Sudan
countries.triviaFact: On July 9, 2011, after decades of civil war and an overwhelming independence vote, this East-Central African nation became the newest internationally recognized sovereign country in the world. The White Nile flows north through the center of the country and spreads out to form the Sudd, one of the largest tropical freshwater wetlands on Earth. Every year, more than a million white-eared kob, tiang, and Mongalla gazelles cross its savannas and floodplains in one of the largest mammal migrations on the planet.

countries.name: São Tomé and Príncipe
countries.officialName: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe
aliases: República Democrática de São Tomé e Príncipe
countries.triviaFact: Two volcanic islands sitting right on the equator in the Gulf of Guinea off Central Africa form the second-smallest sovereign country on the African continent. Rising out of the southern jungle of the main island is Pico Cão Grande, a dramatic needle-shaped plug of dark volcanic rock that shoots more than 300 meters straight above the treetops. In the early 1900s, its rich volcanic soil made it the largest producer of cocoa in the world, and in 1919 astronomer Arthur Eddington photographed a solar eclipse on the smaller island to prove Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity.

countries.name: Suriname
countries.triviaFact: Tucked on the northeastern shoulder of South America between Guyana and French Guiana, this is the smallest independent country on the continent and the only nation outside Europe where Dutch is the official language. More than ninety percent of its territory is covered by untouched primary Amazonian rainforest, making it one of the most forested and carbon-negative countries on Earth. Its coastal capital features historic white wooden colonial buildings and a main street where a grand synagogue and a large mosque stand peacefully side by side.

countries.name: Slovakia
countries.triviaFact: Carved by the jagged granite peaks of the High Tatras in the north and the Danube River in the south, this landlocked Central European country peacefully split from Czechia on New Year's Day in 1993. More than 180 medieval castles and four hundred manor houses dot its hills, including the sprawling stone ruins of Spiš Castle, giving it the highest number of castles per person in the world. Over six thousand karst caves lie beneath its mountains, and its factories assemble more cars per resident than any other country on Earth.

countries.name: Slovenia
countries.triviaFact: Roughly the size of New Jersey, this green Central European country packs the Julian Alps, the Pannonian plains, and a short Adriatic coast into a small space where more than half the land is forest. Its limestone plateau gave science the word 'karst', and visitors ride an underground electric train into Postojna Cave to see blind cave salamanders locals call baby dragons. Picture-book Lake Bled in the northwest features a tiny island church ringed by mountains and a medieval castle perched on a sheer cliff above the water.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.triviaFact: Stretching for more than 1,500 kilometers down the eastern side of the Scandinavian Peninsula, this Nordic kingdom is covered in spruce forests, over 95,000 lakes, and tens of thousands of coastal islands. Its capital is built across fourteen islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic Sea and houses the Vasa Museum, where a 17th-century oak warship raised nearly intact from the harbor floor stands on display. Following the will of dynamite inventor Alfred Nobel, the country awards the Nobel Prizes every December and is famous for flat-pack furniture, pop music exports, and the right to roam freely in nature.

countries.name: Eswatini
countries.triviaFact: Surrounded almost entirely by South Africa with a short border along Mozambique, this small mountainous kingdom in Southern Africa is one of the last absolute monarchies in the world. Inside its northwestern border sits the Ngwenya Mine, where red hematite ochre was mined over forty thousand years ago, making it the oldest known mine in human history. Every late summer, tens of thousands of young women gather in traditional beadwork for the Umhlanga Reed Dance, while wildlife parks protect black and white rhinos.

countries.name: Sint Maarten
countries.triviaFact: Occupying the southern forty percent of a small Caribbean island shared peacefully with France since 1648, this constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands is a busy cruise ship and yachting hub. Right next to Maho Beach lies the main international runway, where jumbo jets fly just a few meters above sunbathers' heads before touching down. Inland salt pans once drove the early Dutch colonial economy, and duty-free waterfront shops line the narrow sandbar of Philipsburg.

countries.name: Seychelles
countries.triviaFact: One hundred and fifteen granite and coral islands lie scattered in the western Indian Ocean north of Madagascar, forming the smallest population of any sovereign African country. Unlike almost all other oceanic islands, which are volcanic or coral, the inner islands are made of ancient pink-gray granite boulders left behind when India broke away from Gondwana millions of years ago. On Praslin Island grows the prehistoric Vallée de Mai palm forest, home to the giant double-coconut Coco de Mer, the heaviest seed in the plant kingdom, while giant Aldabra tortoises roam the outer atolls.

countries.name: Syria
countries.triviaFact: Stretching from the Mediterranean coast across the Orontes and Euphrates river valleys in the heart of the Fertile Crescent, this country contains two of the oldest continuously inhabited cities on Earth in its capital and Aleppo. Out in the central desert stand the monumental colonnades of ancient Palmyra, while the 12th-century stone fortress of Krak des Chevaliers sits on a green hilltop near the coast. For thousands of years, its artisans and farmers have been known for damask silk weaving, Aleppo laurel soap, and pistachio orchards.

countries.name: Turks and Caicos Islands
countries.triviaFact: Forty low-lying coral islands and cays southeast of the Bahamas form this British Overseas Territory, split by a deep ocean trench into two distinct island groups. It takes its name from the indigenous barrel cactus, whose red top looks like an Ottoman fez hat, and the Lucayan word for a string of islands. Grace Bay on Providenciales is famous for twelve miles of powdery white sand protected by one of the longest barrier reefs in the Atlantic.

countries.name: Chad
countries.triviaFact: Stretching from the Sahara Desert in the north through the dry Sahel to fertile savannas in the south, this large landlocked nation sits at the crossroads of North and Central Africa. In the northern Tibesti Mountains rises Emi Koussi, a 3,445-meter extinct volcano that is the highest peak in the entire Sahara, alongside the natural sandstone arches and crocodile waterholes of the Ennedi Plateau. Its namesake shallow freshwater lake on the western border has shrunk by roughly ninety percent since the 1960s, though it still supports millions of farmers and fishermen.

countries.name: Togo
countries.triviaFact: Less than sixty kilometers wide along the Gulf of Guinea, this narrow West African country stretches 550 kilometers inland through coastal lagoons, coffee hills, and northern savannas. In the northern mountains of Koutammakou, the Batammariba people build remarkable two-story mud-and-thatch fortress houses called Takienta that look like miniature castles. The country is also one of the world's leading producers of phosphate rock used in agricultural fertilizers.

countries.name: Thailand
countries.triviaFact: Situated in the heart of mainland Southeast Asia, this kingdom was the only country in the region never colonized by a European power. Gilded Buddhist temples with multi-tiered roofs and giant reclining Buddhas fill the bustling canal-crossed capital and the ancient brick ruins of Ayutthaya and Sukhothai. From the forested hills of the north to the towering limestone sea cliffs and white beaches of the Andaman coast, it is beloved worldwide for its balance of sweet, sour, salty, and spicy street food.

countries.name: Tajikistan
countries.triviaFact: Jagged mountains of the Pamir and Alay ranges cover more than ninety percent of this landlocked Central Asian country, with half of its territory sitting over three thousand meters above sea level. High in the Pamirs, often called the Roof of the World, lies the 77-kilometer Fedchenko Glacier, the longest glacier on Earth outside the polar regions. Unlike its Turkic-speaking Central Asian neighbors, the people here speak a variety of Persian closely related to the language of classical poets like Rudaki and Ferdowsi.

countries.name: Tokelau
countries.triviaFact: Three small coral atolls in the South Pacific halfway between Hawaii and New Zealand form this dependent territory of New Zealand, with only about 1,500 residents. There is no airport, no harbor for large ships, and no cars to speak of, so the only way to reach the islands is a twenty-four-hour boat ride from Samoa. In 2012, the territory made history by installing thousands of solar panels and coconut-oil backup generators to become the first territory in the world powered almost entirely by solar energy.

countries.name: Turkmenistan
countries.triviaFact: Roughly eighty percent of this Central Asian country is covered by the black sands of the Karakum Desert, stretching east from the shore of the Caspian Sea. In the middle of the desert burns the Darvaza gas crater, a seventy-meter-wide collapsed pit where natural gas has been flaming non-stop since Soviet geologists lit it in 1971. Its capital holds the world record for the highest density of white marble-clad buildings, and the country reveres the metallic-sheened Akhal-Teke horse as its national emblem.

countries.name: Timor-Leste
countries.triviaFact: Occupying the eastern half of a mountainous island at the southeastern edge of the Indonesian archipelago, this country became the first new sovereign state of the 21st century in May 2002. Together with the Philippines, it is one of only two predominantly Catholic nations in Asia, a legacy of four centuries of Portuguese colonial rule. Offshore, the deep waters of the Ombai-Wetar Strait sit inside the Coral Triangle and serve as a major migration superhighway for blue whales and sperm whales.

countries.name: Tonga
countries.triviaFact: More than 170 islands spread across the South Pacific form the only island nation in the region that never lost its indigenous sovereignty to a foreign colonial power. It is still governed by a constitutional monarch whose royal line stretches back over a thousand years, and Captain James Cook famously marveled at the warm hospitality of its islanders in 1773. Just west of the International Date Line, its coral reefs and blowhole cliffs are a prime winter breeding sanctuary for southern humpback whales.

countries.name: Trinidad and Tobago
countries.triviaFact: Situated just eleven kilometers off the coast of Venezuela at the southern end of the Caribbean chain, this two-island republic sits on the South American continental shelf. In the 20th century, musicians here hammered discarded oil drums into tuned steelpans, the only new non-electric acoustic musical instrument invented in the 1900s, and created calypso and soca music for its world-famous Carnival. On the southwestern coast of the larger island lies La Brea Pitch Lake, the largest natural deposit of liquid asphalt on Earth.

countries.name: Tunisia
countries.triviaFact: Containing the northernmost point on the African continent, this compact country stretches from sunny Mediterranean olive groves and beaches down into the Sahara Desert. Just outside its modern capital lie the seaside ruins of the ancient Phoenician empire whose general Hannibal famously crossed the Alps with elephants to challenge Rome, alongside the huge Roman amphitheater at El Jem. In the dry south, Berber families carved cool underground courtyard homes into the soft sandstone hills of Matmata, which later served as a filming location for Star Wars.

countries.name: Türkiye
countries.triviaFact: Bridging Southeastern Europe and Western Asia across the narrow Bosphorus Strait, this transcontinental republic sits on a peninsula that hosted the Hittite, Greek, Roman, Byzantine, and Ottoman empires. In southeastern Anatolia stands Göbekli Tepe, a ring of carved T-shaped stone pillars built around 9600 BCE that is the oldest known monumental temple site on Earth. Visitors also explore the domes of Hagia Sophia, the white travertine hot-spring terraces of Pamukkale, and the cone-shaped volcanic rock valleys of Cappadocia.

countries.name: Tuvalu
countries.triviaFact: Nine tiny low-lying coral atolls and reef islands in the South Pacific midway between Hawaii and Australia form the fourth-smallest independent country in the world. Covering only twenty-six square kilometers in total and rising less than five meters above sea level at its highest point, the narrow strips of land are heavily threatened by rising ocean tides. Because its international internet country code happens to be '.tv', leasing that domain name to streaming and media companies generates nearly ten percent of the government's total annual revenue.

countries.name: Taiwan
countries.triviaFact: Shaped like a tobacco leaf off the southeastern coast of mainland Asia, this mountainous island has nearly three hundred peaks rising over 3,000 meters, including Jade Mountain, and the sheer marble walls of Taroko Gorge. Its high-tech factories produce the majority of the world's most advanced computer microchips, making the island essential to global electronics. By night, lantern-lit street markets buzz with stalls serving beef noodle soup, soup dumplings, and chewy tapioca bubble tea, which was invented here in the 1980s.

countries.name: Tanzania
countries.triviaFact: Formed in 1964 by uniting the mainland territory of Tanganyika with the spice islands of Zanzibar, this East African nation holds both the highest and lowest points on the continent. Snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro rises 5,895 meters as the tallest freestanding mountain in the world, while the fossil-rich gorge of Olduvai yielded some of the earliest known human ancestor remains. Across the northern plains, the Serengeti and the giant volcanic bowl of Ngorongoro Crater protect millions of lions, elephants, rhinos, and migrating wildebeest.

countries.name: Uganda
countries.triviaFact: Straddling the equator in the Great Rift Valley, this fertile landlocked nation is where the White Nile flows out of Lake Victoria, Africa's largest lake, and squeezes through a narrow seven-meter rock cleft at Murchison Falls. Along the western border rise the snow-capped Rwenzori Mountains, while the thick mists of Bwindi Impenetrable Forest shelter roughly half of the world's remaining mountain gorillas. With one of the youngest populations in the world, the country is also a leading producer of Robusta coffee and cooking bananas called matooke.

countries.name: Ukraine
countries.triviaFact: Covering more than 600,000 square kilometers north of the Black Sea, this is the largest country whose borders lie entirely within Europe. Roughly a third of the world's richest black topsoil, called chernozem, blankets its flat steppes, earning it the title of the Breadbasket of Europe for its massive harvests of wheat, corn, and sunflower oil. Gold-domed cathedrals like Saint Sophia and the ancient cave monastery of Pechersk Lavra have stood above the Dnieper River in its capital for nearly a thousand years.

countries.name: United States Minor Outlying Islands
aliases: Baker, Howland, Jarvis, Johnston, Kingman, Midway, Palmyra, Wake, Navassa
countries.triviaFact: Eight isolated coral island groups in the Pacific Ocean and Navassa Island in the Caribbean make up this statistical collection of unincorporated United States territories. None of the islands have any permanent civilian residents, though Midway Atoll played a turning-point role in World War II naval history and Wake Island hosts a small airfield team. Today, almost all of these tiny atolls and surrounding reefs are protected as national wildlife refuges for millions of nesting seabirds, green sea turtles, and monk seals.

countries.name: Uruguay
countries.triviaFact: Rolling grassy plains called pampas cover most of this compact South American country wedged between Argentina and Brazil along the Atlantic coast. Cattle outnumber the 3.4 million human residents by nearly four to one, and the country became a pioneer in social welfare, secular education, and generating almost one hundred percent of its electricity from wind, solar, and hydropower. In 1930, its capital hosted and won the very first FIFA World Cup tournament in football history.

countries.name: United States
countries.triviaFact: Spanning from the Atlantic to the Pacific across fifty states, plus Alaska in the Arctic and the volcanic Hawaiian archipelago, this is the third-largest country in the world in both area and population. In 1872, it established Yellowstone as the world's first national park, part of a natural landscape that includes the mile-deep Grand Canyon, giant sequoia trees, and the Mississippi River basin. From putting the first astronauts on the Moon and inventing the airplane and internet to Hollywood cinema, jazz, rock, and hip-hop, its innovations have shaped the modern world.

countries.name: Uzbekistan
countries.triviaFact: Along with tiny Liechtenstein, this Central Asian nation is one of only two doubly landlocked countries on Earth, meaning you must cross at least two borders to reach an ocean. For over a thousand years, its oasis cities of Samarkand, Bukhara, and Khiva stood at the heart of the Silk Road, leaving behind dazzling plazas of turquoise-tiled domes and minarets like the Registan. It was also the homeland of medieval mathematician Al-Khwarizmi, whose name gave us the words algebra and algorithm, and astronomer Ulugh Beg.

countries.name: Vatican City
countries.triviaFact: Covering just forty-four hectares behind medieval stone walls inside Rome, this is the smallest independent state in the world in both area and population. Ruled by the Pope as the spiritual center of the Roman Catholic Church, it has its own post office, radio station, railway spur, and colorful Swiss Guard corps founded in 1506. Millions of visitors pass through its gates each year to stand beneath the massive dome of Saint Peter's Basilica and admire Michelangelo's painted ceiling inside the Sistine Chapel.

countries.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
countries.triviaFact: One mountainous volcanic main island and a chain of thirty-one smaller coral and volcanic islands stretch southward across the eastern Caribbean Sea. On the main island, the active volcano La Soufrière rises over 1,200 meters above black-sand beaches and the oldest botanical garden in the Western Hemisphere, founded in 1765. Farther south, yachts sail through the clear turquoise reefs and sea turtle sanctuaries of the Tobago Cays and Mustique.

countries.name: Venezuela
countries.triviaFact: Located on the northern coast of South America, this country holds the largest proven crude oil reserves in the world and a dramatic landscape where the Andes meet the Caribbean and the Orinoco basin. In the southeastern Canaima jungle, flat-topped sandstone tabletop mountains called tepuis rise out of the clouds, and water plunges 979 meters off Auyán-tepui at Angel Falls, the highest uninterrupted waterfall on Earth. Over Lake Maracaibo in the northwest, warm mountain winds create the Catatumbo lightning phenomenon, where thousands of lightning bolts flash almost every night.

countries.name: British Virgin Islands
countries.triviaFact: About sixty volcanic islands and small cays in the northeastern Caribbean make up this overseas territory of the United Kingdom, known as one of the premier sailing capitals of the world. On the second-largest island, giant rounded granite boulders sit piled along the beach at The Baths, forming sunlit saltwater grottos and natural rock pools. The territory is also famous for sunken shipwrecks like the RMS Rhone and uses the United States dollar as its official currency.

countries.name: United States Virgin Islands
countries.officialName: Virgin Islands of the United States
countries.triviaFact: Purchased by the United States from Denmark in 1917 to protect the approaches to the Panama Canal, this territory consists of the three main islands of Saint Thomas, Saint Croix, and Saint John. It is the only place under United States jurisdiction where drivers travel on the left side of the road, even though almost all cars have American left-hand steering wheels. Two-thirds of Saint John is protected as a national park of coral bays and forested trails, while old stone sugar-mill towers still dot Saint Croix.

countries.name: Vietnam
aliases: Cộng hòa Xã hội chủ nghĩa Việt Nam
countries.triviaFact: Curving like the letter S along the eastern edge of the Indochinese Peninsula, this Southeast Asian country stretches from the terraced mountains of the north to the fertile Mekong Delta in the south. Over 1,600 tree-covered limestone pillars rise out of the emerald waters of Ha Long Bay, while the central jungle hides Son Doong, the largest natural cave passage in the world by volume. As one of the world's top exporters of coffee, rice, and cashews, the country is famous for its street scooter traffic, lantern-lit Hoi An, and aromatic pho noodle soup.

countries.name: Vanuatu
countries.triviaFact: Roughly eighty volcanic islands stretch in a Y-shape across the South Pacific, where glowing lava lakes bubble continuously inside active craters like Mount Yasur on Tanna. On Pentecost Island, young men tie forest vines to their ankles and leap from tall wooden towers in a ritual called Naghol to bless the yam harvest, the ancient tradition that inspired modern bungee jumping. Citizens speak Bislama, a colorful English-based creole, alongside more than a hundred local indigenous languages.

countries.name: Wallis and Futuna
countries.officialName: Territory of the Wallis and Futuna Islands
countries.triviaFact: Two separate volcanic island groups about 260 kilometers apart in the South Pacific between Fiji and Samoa make up this French overseas collectivity. Uniquely within the French Republic, three traditional Polynesian kings still rule alongside the French territorial administrator and hold official status in local custom and law. On the main island of Uvea, a nearly circular volcanic crater lake called Lalolalo drops straight down eighty meters inside a ring of thick jungle.

countries.name: Samoa
countries.triviaFact: Two large volcanic islands, Savai'i and Upolu, along with several smaller islets in the heart of Polynesia, became the first Pacific island nation to gain independence in 1962. Daily village life is still guided by Fa'a, a three-thousand-year-old code of family respect, open-sided round houses called fale, and traditional hand-tapped tattooing. On the southern coast of Upolu, swimmers climb down a wooden ladder into the To-Sua Ocean Trench, a thirty-meter-deep collapse pool fed by underground sea lava tubes.

countries.name: Yemen
countries.triviaFact: Sitting at the southwestern corner of the Arabian Peninsula along the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, this mountainous land was famous in ancient Rome because its high peaks caught monsoon rains and grew rich harvests of coffee and frankincense. In the desert valley of Wadi Hadhramaut stands Shibam, a 16th-century walled town of seven-story mud-brick apartment towers often called the Manhattan of the Desert, while terraced stone houses line the old capital. Out in the Indian Ocean lies its island of Socotra, famous for umbrella-shaped Dragon's Blood trees that bleed red sap and grow nowhere else on Earth.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.triviaFact: Wrapping around the southern tip of the continent where the cold Atlantic and warm Indian oceans meet, this nation recognizes twelve official languages, including English, Zulu, Xhosa, Afrikaans, and Sign Language. Uniquely, it splits its government across three separate capital cities: one for the executive branch, one beneath flat-topped Table Mountain for parliament, and a third in the central plains for the supreme court. In 1994, anti-apartheid leader Nelson Mandela became its first democratically elected president, and nearby limestone caves hold some of the richest early hominin fossils on Earth.

countries.name: Zambia
countries.triviaFact: Rich copper mines across the northern plateau drive the economy of this landlocked Southern African country, which takes its name from the great river flowing along its southern border. On that border, the river plunges more than a hundred meters into a narrow basalt chasm at Victoria Falls, called Mosi-oa-Tunya, or the Smoke That Thunders, forming the largest curtain of falling water in the world. Its national parks, such as South Luangwa and Kafue, pioneered the walking safari and shelter huge populations of hippos, leopards, and elephants.

countries.name: Zimbabwe
countries.triviaFact: High granite plateaus and balancing rock formations shape this landlocked Southern African nation situated between the Zambezi and Limpopo rivers. The country takes its name from a medieval royal city of the 11th to 15th centuries whose massive granite walls and conical tower were stacked entirely without mortar, forming the largest ancient stone structure in sub-Saharan Africa. Alongside sharing the thunderous mist of Victoria Falls and Lake Kariba, the world's largest man-made reservoir by volume, the country is famous for Shona stone sculpture.
